rule: Name the reader and the decision before any display is designed
why: A display for nobody serves nobody; the first feature of an actionable dashboard
source: Ivanković et al. 2021†; Jivet et al. 2018

rule: State the dashboard's job — monitor, analyse or communicate — in writing, and design for it
why: The three jobs need different displays; most are used to communicate

rule: Document provenance, method, positionality and uncertainty on the face of the display
why: A dashboard is a translator; its readers must be able to check it
source: Kitchin et al. 2015; O'Neill 2002; Code of Practice

rule: Release the data with the display, through a documented route
why: A dashboard without a data release is a wall downstream

rule: Show uncertainty as a numeric range, never as a vague hedge or a hidden point
why: Numeric uncertainty costs almost no trust; verbal hedging does

rule: Design and measure use from the first day
why: Non-use is the dominant failure mode and is almost never measured
source: Dowding et al. 2015; Rossi et al. 2025

rule: Watch for the proxy moving without the goal; measure the goal where it can be measured
why: Dashboards move the countable before the intended
source: Jivet et al. 2018; Kaliisa et al. 2024†; Gerrish 2016†

rule: Treat every published measure as reactive; audit for gaming
why: A measure that becomes a target ceases to be a good measure

rule: Show and justify the unit of aggregation; test sensitivity to it
why: The same numbers regrouped can give any answer

rule: Scale size-dependent measures by an appropriate denominator, and say which
why: Unscaled sums are won by the big

rule: Rankings by rate are screening instruments, never verdicts; show intervals
why: Two-thirds of comparisons in a typical league table cannot be separated; small units sit at both ends

rule: Where official statistics suppress or perturb, show that fact, never a blank
why: Suppression removes exactly the small cells a local reader needs

rule: Investigate an outlier as a mechanism before treating it as noise; use positive deviance as a method
why: A favourable outlier is the object of study, not the thing to trim

rule: Treat trust as earned by conduct — trustworthiness, quality, value — not sought from the display
why: Trust attaches to the producer and detaches from the presenter
source: Code of Practice; Public Confidence in Official Statistics 2023

rule: Build the common ground before the screen; test recognition with each community
why: A boundary object is a social achievement, not a design feature
tier: Adaptable in method; Fixed as sequence

rule: Where the measure is of a place, think multilevel: the place is information, not only an average
why: Both the ecological and the atomistic fallacy are real

rule: Never print an unsourced adoption or failure percentage for dashboards
why: None exists that is independent

rule: The job, the layering, the degree of framing, the order of failures to prevent, the amount of mud
why: Open choices with named trade-offs

rule: Register, imagery, metaphor
why: Free, within the design system

rule: Name each reader, the decision they make, the evidence they are obliged to accept and the clock they keep, before design; declare whose grammar the first screen speaks
why: Readers grade by contradictory rules; the first screen is always in somebody's grammar; a display built for a reader in general is graded by none

rule: Label every panel as monitoring or as evaluation; never imply a counterfactual the display does not have
why: The official reader's grammar makes the distinction and discounts the breach

rule: State where a claim stands on the evidence ladder when it will be read by a funder or a What Works body
why: A before-and-after is Maryland Level 1; data showing change is Nesta Level 2; the reader will score it so

rule: Follow the Treasury's order — monetise, quantify, describe — and label which is which; never present a benefit-cost ratio as the decision
why: The order is mandatory guidance; the ratio is not the decision

rule: Any wellbeing value carries its design grade and its range (£10,000–£16,000 per WELLBY)
why: The Treasury grades wellbeing evidence by causal design

rule: Show "who benefits" — distribution across groups and places — as a panel, not a footnote
why: Distributional analysis is now a required question

rule: Show the reader's own geography — the ward, the patch — at the scale they plan at
why: Local beats rigorous; the member's evidence is their ward

rule: Make the source checkable before making the chart persuasive
why: Readers triage by source credibility first and do not sort by method

rule: Design release to the reader's calendar; keep the problem documented between windows
why: Timing is the most prominent barrier and a strategy, not a circumstance
source: Oliver 2014; Cairney & Kwiatkowski 2017; Kingdon via Mintrom & True

rule: Offer a plain-table view as a first-class route for the reader already opposed
why: In one study, tables out-persuaded charts among the hostile in all three topics; the authors call the result uncertain

rule: Never add a chart for its air of science; add it for the information it carries
why: The trivial-graph effect did not replicate; and the design system's own rule that strong design must never make weak evidence look stronger

rule: Name the denominator on every map and comparison, and show the alternative
why: Count versus rate moved perception by nine points; the fraction of a group is the persuasive unit

rule: Treat a league table as acting on the ranked; never present one as a reader's decision aid without intervals
why: Public performance data barely moves consumer choice and reorganises the ranked
source: Cochrane 2018; Marshall et al. 2000†; Espeland & Sauder 2007; Ch 1

rule: Show uncertainty as a numeric range; never as a verbal hedge; never omit it to protect the signal
why: Numeric ranges cost almost nothing at n = 10,519; omission is an editorial choice

rule: Never let a place indicator be read as evidence of an intervention; mark descriptions as descriptions
why: Fuzzy concept, proxy data, rewards the already-successful

rule: Define the construct before choosing the proxy
why: Or the proxy defines it

rule: Carry every valuation's caveats on the face of the display
why: The next release will drop them; this is the last place they survive

rule: Decide openly whose reading a property-value or footfall figure serves, and show the choice
why: Success to the investor; displacement to the resident

rule: Claim outputs and outcomes for organisations; claim impact only at the level that can see the system
why: Impact belongs to funders, coalitions and places

rule: Release numbers with their data and caveats so an opposing coalition's analyst can check them
why: Cross-coalition learning needs shared, checkable figures
source: Sabatier via Cairney; Code of Practice (Ch 1)

rule: Agree data standards and the route to decision with the scene before collecting
why: Community data earns standing when both are co-agreed first

rule: Do not place lived experience in a panel beside the numbers as a supplement
why: That is the re-filing three Scottish cases describe
tier: Adaptable in form; Fixed as a prohibition on the supplement pattern

rule: Recognition is checked before release, as a dialogue that can change the next release
why: Member checking is a credibility test only when it can alter the account

rule: Numbers for understanding, not numbers for advocacy: produce with caveats, release with data
why: A sector's dashboard is read by the people advocacy numbers are used against

rule: Which reader comes first (declared); monetise/quantify/describe; the plain-table view; where lived experience sits; which numbers the investor sees; documenting between windows
why: Open choices with named trade-offs

rule: Register, imagery, metaphor
why: Free, within the design system

rule: Name the comparison the reader is to make before choosing a form; design the display to make that comparison first
why: Statistics are fast, comparisons slow and serial; design works by choosing the comparison
source: Franconeri et al. 2021; Ajani et al. 2022 (n = 24)

rule: For a precise ratio comparison, use position on a common scale, then length; do not ask for a precise reading from area or colour
why: Replicated top of the hierarchy
tier: **Fixed** for precise comparison; Adaptable as a general form rule

rule: Never let colour be the only means of distinguishing or conveying anything
why: Level A success criterion; 8% of men

rule: Text at 4.5:1; parts of graphics needed to understand the content at 3:1 against adjacent colours
why: Level AA

rule: Lightness for order, hue for category; no rainbow for ordered data on a pattern map
why: Lightness is read as order; the rainbow bins and exaggerates
tier: **Fixed** (pattern maps); Adaptable where the task is reading a value
source: Liu & Heer 2018; Franconeri 2021; Reda et al. 2018

rule: Limit categorical colours — seven is the experimental ceiling for search, four or five the house limit; give small marks bigger colour steps
why: Search degrades beyond seven; small marks need bigger differences than large ones

rule: Put the message in the title, in words; put statistics and context beside the marks; never title-only, never no-text
why: Title first, longest, remembered, decisive; readers prefer the most-annotated chart; placement follows meaning
source: Borkin et al. 2016; Kong et al. 2018; Stokes et al. 2023

rule: Title and chart point at the same salient thing
why: A caption cannot redirect to a faint feature; a contradicting title is believed and unnoticed
source: Kim, Setlur & Agrawala 2021; Kong et al. 2019

rule: Label at the mark; legends only where labels cannot fit, and then ordered to match the data
why: Working-memory round trip; spatial contiguity d = 0.72; the compliance route for 1.4.1

rule: Build first screens from fast-glance forms; avoid radial bars for comparison
why: Six-fold glance penalty for the decorative form — from 36 people on a smartwatch

rule: Design the first glance for simplicity and for looking like what the display claims to be
why: Appeal forms in 50 ms on complexity and prototypicality — websites, small student samples
tier: Adaptable (what it claims to be is Carly's)
source: Lindgaard et al. 2006; Tuch et al. 2012

rule: Pictograms that are the data are permitted; nothing decorative behind the data; no styled bars (rounded, capped, triangular)
why: Free or helpful; distracting; inaccurate, respectively
source: Haroz et al. 2015; Skau et al. 2015

rule: Declutter for professionalism; add a headline, one highlight and one sentence for recall
why: 2.5–3× recall of the intended conclusion in one study of 24; consistent with the title and text evidence; trust unmoved by either
tier: Adaptable (strong default); the headline itself is Fixed under the words rule
source: Ajani et al. 2022; Borkin et al. 2016; Stokes et al. 2023

rule: Bar axes start at zero; a broken line axis is declared and the effect size it implies is chosen deliberately
why: Truncation exaggerates even when labelled and taught
source: Correll et al. 2020; Yang et al. 2021†; Long & Kay 2024

rule: Do not compare non-baseline segments of a stacked bar; use grouped or dot charts
why: Length judgement plus part-of-whole bias

rule: Public defaults: linear scale, daily flow with the cumulative available, absolute risk with a fixed denominator and a stated interval
why: Log halved correct reading of one question; cumulative raises perceived risk; relative risk persuades without informing; 1-in-X alarms (health domain)
source: Romano et al. 2020†; Reinholtz et al. 2021; Akl et al. 2011; Pighin et al. 2011†

rule: Show a value the reader wants to know as a number or a table, not a chart; show a trend or comparison as a chart
why: Cognitive fit

rule: Two or three significant figures; never more precision than the data has; frequencies ("9 in 100") where chance is involved
why: Readers round anyway; precision reads as confidence; frequencies are reasoned about better
source: Ehrenberg 1977; Cole 2015; Gigerenzer & Hoffrage 1995; McDowell & Jacobs 2017

rule: Nothing crucial behind a click, a hover or a tooltip; everything crucial reachable by keyboard and on a phone
why: Median use of optional controls is zero (interactive articles, not dashboards); hover does not exist on touch; SC 2.1.1

rule: Every default — place, measure, period, sort, extent — is chosen, written down and shown as a choice
why: Defaults shift choices (d = 0.68, policy and consumer domains), partly by being read as advice; the opening view anchors the session
source: Jachimowicz et al. 2019; Cho et al. 2017; Hullman & Diakopoulos 2011

rule: Treat "overview first" as a satisfaction preference; let the reader's arriving question decide
why: 52 citations, no validations; 2 of 17 comparisons more accurate

rule: Small multiples for analysis; animation only for transitions between states of the same chart, or for presentation with the static version available
why: Animation enjoyed, slower, less accurate; transitions preserve identity
source: Robertson et al. 2008; Heer & Robertson 2007; Brehmer et al. 2019

rule: Never a bare interval or a hard boundary for uncertainty; prefer countable dots, gradients, violins or animated draws; show outcome spread, not only estimate uncertainty, where individuals are the subject
why: Within-the-bar bias; containment; CI overstates individual effect (a treatment-effect game, n > 3,500)
source: Correll & Gleicher 2014; Padilla et al. 2017; Hofman et al. 2020; Kay et al. 2016

rule: A word for probability carries its number in brackets beside it
why: 32% → 66% agreement; a glossary does not help
source: Wintle et al. 2019; Budescu et al. 2014

rule: Test uncertainty displays with sceptical readers before release
why: One study: uncertainty may amplify discounting among the strongly opposed

rule: Plan for a reader at PIAAC Level 1 and with low graph literacy; test with them
why: A fifth of adults in England; a third with both deficits in Germany and the US

rule: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA as the yardstick of reasonable adjustment; two-part text alternatives for every chart; `role="img"` or `graphics-document` on every SVG chart
why: Equality Act anticipatory duty; WAI complex-images guidance; no chart role exists
source: Equality Act 2010 s.20; WCAG 2.2; WAI tutorials; WAI-ARIA 1.2

rule: Which chart below the top of the hierarchy; how many colours; how much text; convention or novelty at first glance; which uncertainty form; line-axis breaks; overview or search; animation or multiples; rounding
why: Open choices with named trade-offs

rule: Register, imagery, metaphor, texture around the chart
why: Free, within the design system and provided nothing that carries meaning lives only there

rule: State the unit of observation (what one row is) and the count of rows beneath every figure
why: The grain is a choice that changes the count; three units (reporting, observation, statistical) are routinely conflated; the row count is our reading of what the figure needs to bear weight

rule: State the reference period as a closed interval, separately from the date issued and the date last modified
why: A number has three dates; the stamp usually gives the least useful

rule: Write down the rule by which an activity that crosses a boundary (midnight; month end; clock change) is assigned to a period; never change it without a [b]
why: The boundary is a measurement rule and decides how much is counted
tier: **Fixed** as a stance; the rule itself Adaptable
source: KH03; Pierce et al. 2024 (secondary); Eurostat calendar adjustment

rule: ISO 8601 with UTC offset in data; natural dates in display
why: Sorts correctly as text; removes ambiguity; a day across a clock change is not 24 hours

rule: Name the denominator of every rate and make the alternatives reachable; use time-in-observation (person-time, venue-nights) where units are observed for unequal spans
why: A rate exists to compare unequal populations; the reference class is a choice

rule: Rates on small bases carry intervals and are shown in a funnel, never ranked raw or ranked adjusted
why: Small units fill both tails; shrinkage flips the artefact

rule: Ship the provenance set with every figure: responsible party; source and why; method and deviations; period; issued and modified; status; quality with error; what was withheld; what it may be compared with
why: The regulator's list, the European dimensions and three machine standards converge on it
source: Code of Practice 3.0 Std 6, 7, 3.9, 3.10, 4.5, 9.3, 9.5, 10.5; Reg. 223/2009; PROV-DM; DCAT 3; FAIR R1.2

rule: Keep the record when the number changes: a figure's description and its previous values outlive its current value
why: Metadata "accessible, even when the data are no longer available"; revisions are normal and should be visible in one place
source: FAIR A2; OSR 2023 on GDP revisions

rule: Use "reliable" in the official sense (closeness of early to later estimates) or not at all; show provisional figures as [p] and revised as [r]
why: The ordinary and official senses diverge

rule: Name who owns the display's figures and who assured them; assure in proportion to the weight of the decision
why: Four roles; a single responsible owner; fit for *this* purpose

rule: Zero only for a true zero; never for missing, rounded-to-zero or not-applicable
why: The data-standard, the statistical standard and the relational model agree
source: Analysis Function; Eurostat "0n"; SDMX N; Codd 1986

rule: Every empty cell states its kind; a blank is permitted only where there is exactly one reason for blanks and it is stated above the table
why: More than one kind of nothing forces a label on every nothing

rule: Never "NA", "N/A" or a bare symbol as the label for a nothing; letters in square brackets, or words
why: Ambiguous between not applicable and not available; symbols defeat screen readers

rule: Distinguish *not applicable* (the value cannot exist) from *not asked* (it could, and nobody did)
why: Every official scheme makes the split; the studio's six do not
tier: Adaptable (how to name it) — flagged for Carly
source: SDMX M/L; [z]/[x]; Codd I/A-mark; Understanding Society −8

rule: Treat "free" as a value — zero price with a quantity — and never as a nothing; make the quantity visible where the price is zero
why: The national statistician's price-index method; no scheme codes it as missing
kind: Standard (adjacent domain — price indices) + Nightlife Culture

rule: Never join a line across a missing point, dotted or dashed; highlight the gap and say why
why: "Joining points implies we know something about the data"

rule: Flag every imputed or estimated value as such, with the method and who estimated; show imputation rates
why: Filled values carry uncertainty measured values do not

rule: A suppressed cell is marked, never blanked; secondary suppression applied; the display states whether its protection is suppression or perturbation
why: A blank is six things; a perturbed table is quietly [e]
source: Analysis Function SDC; Code 4.5; ONS Census 2021

rule: Where the mechanism of missingness may be correlated with the measure, show what would change if the nothing were something
why: MAR cannot be verified from data; sensitivity analysis is the remedy

rule: Every comparison carries the ten-line declaration (definition; period; geography and vintage; method; disclosure; breaks; revisions; comparator and method; precision; outlier handling)
why: Valid "to the extent that differences … can be attributed to differences between the true values"
source: SIMS/SDMX glossary; Reg. 223/2009; European Code P14; Code 3.0; ESMA 2015

rule: Mark a change of definition or method with [b]; provide a back series or correction factors where possible
why: Before and after "cannot be directly compared"

rule: Use area codes with their vintage; declare the lookup for any best-fit aggregation; never compare across a boundary change without it
why: Codes change only with boundaries and are never re-used; best-fit carries stated error

rule: A like-for-like or defined measure is defined, reconciled to an audited total, shown with comparators, held constant, and restated if redefined
why: The finance rule, resembling the statistical one

rule: Name the comparator group and publish its variables, standardisation, distance and count; the comparator model must not contain the outcome
why: "The outcome ultimately relies on the indicators and mathematical procedures used"; IMD contains employment at 22.5%

rule: Beside any sum or mean of a skewed quantity, show the median and a concentration measure (top-share, Lorenz curve, Gini or HHI)
why: A total is a weighted statement about its largest terms
source: Lorenz 1905; NIST; ONS ASHE; World Bank; DoJ

rule: Do not assume 80/20; measure the bow
why: Misnamed by its populariser; the shape varies and is more extreme in cultural markets

rule: Where a display ranks by popularity, say so and show the distribution: visible popularity increases concentration and unpredictability
why: Experimental; n = 14,341

rule: Report platform and transactional feeds as within-sample comparisons unless the selection has been measured against a benchmark; state coverage
why: Quality × quantity × difficulty; 2.3 million ≈ 400 at ρ ≈ −0.005

rule: Audit every feed against the ten characteristics and publish the audit with the feed's provenance
why: A ready-made checklist; algorithmic confounding and drift are invisible in the data
tier: Adaptable (strong default; the audit itself is a Nightlife Culture choice)

rule: Never claim what a head-only feed cannot see
why: Top-50 data say nothing about the tail

rule: For administrative sources, state why the organisation recorded it and who is not in it
why: Not collected for research; undocumented for analysis; coverage and unit errors
source: ONS 2023 error catalogue; Connelly et al. 2016

rule: Write the outlier rule and threshold before the data arrives; prefer the median absolute deviation to mean-and-SD; justify the threshold
why: Mean-and-SD is self-defeating; 41% silent-exclusion signal
tier: **Fixed** as a procedure; Adaptable (rule and threshold)

rule: Investigate a flagged point against the six artefact causes before treating it as a finding; remove only a confirmed artefact, and declare the removal
why: The definition is "a different mechanism"; the seventh cause is the finding
source: Hawkins via Aggarwal; Osborne & Overbay 2004; NIST

rule: Any figure shown with a point removed is shown with it included, one tap away
why: "Report what the statistical results are if those observations are included"

rule: Do not run automated outlier alerts on box-plot fences or normal-theory tests for skewed data without stating the false-flag rate
why: ≥30% of normal samples flagged; non-normality read as outliers

rule: Treat a good-end outlier as a hypothesis about mechanism; state the criteria, threshold and comparison group; show its base
why: Positive deviance's second step; its systematic review
source: Bradley et al. 2009; Baxter et al. 2016; Gelman & Price

rule: Contextual anomalies (unusual for this place at this time) need a model of normal that includes the context; a global threshold cannot find them
why: Point, contextual and collective anomalies

rule: Which grain, which day boundary, which denominator, which concentration instrument, whether a seventh kind of nothing, how a nothing looks, how much provenance on the face, suppress or perturb, which outlier rule, which neighbours
why: Open choices with named trade-offs

rule: How the labels, codes, gaps and provenance panels are styled
why: Free within the design system and Chapter 3's rules on colour and words

rule: Write the construct and the theoretical framework before choosing parts; a composite without one is not built
why: The handbook's first step; a "mashup index" is one whose producer "is essentially free to set" its parts

rule: Every part of a composite carries Chapter 4's provenance set
why: A composite inherits every defect of its parts and hides them

rule: State the normalisation and note that it sets exchange rates; prefer the method that matches the data's shape and the measure's purpose
why: Z-scores let extremes dominate; min-max lets outliers set the range; the trade-off changes with the unit

rule: Declare who set the weights and how; treat equal weights as a declared judgement, never a default; check for the uneven-group trap
why: "Weights are essentially value judgements"; "equal weighting does not mean 'no weights'"
source: Handbook §1.6; Greco et al. 2019; SPI methodology

rule: Show the effective importance of each part beside its nominal weight
why: Nominal weights "are hardly ever found to match" main effects; 20% can explain 21% and 40% can explain 81%
source: Paruolo, Saisana & Saltelli 2013; Becker et al. 2017†

rule: Choose the aggregation as a judgement about which parts may compensate which, and say so
why: Addition is fully compensatory; (21,1,1,1) = (6,6,6,6); the HDI, Legatum and the IMD all changed their arithmetic to stop good parts hiding bad ones
source: Handbook §1.6 and toolbox (via JRC web reproduction); HDR 2010; Legatum; IoD 2019

rule: Publish the price list of any additive or partly compensatory index — the rate at which each part exchanges for each other, in the parts' own units — and answer the refusal test
why: The exchange rate exists whether or not it is shown ($0.51 against $9,000); "how many new venues compensate for one forty-year-old institution?"

rule: Decide and declare whether the instrument is one-tailed (built to find shortfall, or thriving) or two-tailed
why: The IMD is "specifically constructed to identify deprivation and not affluence"; the arithmetic differs

rule: Run an uncertainty and sensitivity analysis over the defensible alternatives and publish the rank with its interval
why: "No longer a magic number"; ranks read "not only at face value, but also within the 90 percent confidence intervals"
source: Saisana, Saltelli & Tarantola 2005; JRC GII 2025 audit

rule: Report composite scores to two effective digits unless the inputs justify more; never imply a resolution the inputs lack
why: Official rounding guidance; decimal places are a claim
source: ONS style guide; Analysis Function tables guidance; Ehrenberg (Ch 3)

rule: Say a rank as a range with a most-likely value
why: The official form for an uncertain figure

rule: Design the independent audit with the measure: name the check that is not on the dashboard, its frequency and owner, and the response to gaming
why: Measures change what they measure; the improvements were real and remain unverifiable because no independent check was built

rule: Expect ratchet, threshold and output-distortion effects and the three non-adversarial failures of a proxy; monitor the distribution near any threshold
why: The eight-minute "spike"; regressional, extremal and causal failure need no cheat

rule: Use "multiple indicators, all recognized as imperfect" and never a single target with sanctions attached
why: Campbell's remedy, with his own doubt; the target was met only where it carried sanction, and gamed there

rule: Validate a reading for a use, under the five sources of evidence; state reliability first, including inter-rater reliability for any judged score
why: "It is the interpretations of test scores for proposed uses that are evaluated, not the test itself"

rule: Test discriminant validity against size and against platform coverage
why: A measure that moves with the platform measures the platform

rule: Count a consequence against validity when it traces to construct underrepresentation or irrelevant variance; otherwise record it as a consequence
why: The *Standards'* boundary; Messick's two failures

rule: Cognitively test any felt-quality question before use; present felt qualities as a small panel unless a combination is separately validated
why: The ONS's four questions; "It is not appropriate to combine these questions"
source: ONS QMI and user guide; Dolan, Layard & Metcalfe 2011

rule: Gather recognition from the people measured, record what it corrected, and mark it on the card as face validity and credibility — not as evidence of the construct
why: Member checks correct fact and confirm resonance; evidence that they improve findings is thin; the *Standards* do not count face validity
source: Lincoln & Guba — secondary; Birt et al. 2016; Thomas 2017 — secondary; Morse et al. 2002; Reed 2008

rule: Give the people measured the first claim on which parts count and how they are weighted, through a facilitated process with real decision power
why: The studio's own position, with Sen's argument from public reasoning; the evidence on process design is from environmental management and says how, not whether
kind: Nightlife Culture + Reading; Evidence (adjacent domain) for the how
source: Sen 2005; de Vente et al. 2016; Charlton 1998

rule: Combine community-chosen indicators with field measurement; accept neither unquestioningly
why: Mostly valid, "not always sufficiently accurate or reliable"

rule: Whatever the form, the components travel with it: a composite is accompanied by its dashboard
why: UNECE 2025 recommendation; Stiglitz–Sen–Fitoussi; Paruolo's second option (do not aggregate pillars with important trade-offs)

rule: Publish the recipe as a standard card, one tap from any composed number, with the fact of composition visible beside the number
why: Three of the handbook's six cons are conditional on transparency; "explicit, public steps of inference"
kind: Nightlife Culture + Standard; Practice for the form
source: Version 1 Ch 6; Handbook; Cronbach & Meehl 1955; Gebru et al.; Mitchell et al.; Holland et al.

rule: No composite cultural-value score without an adopted method: the ten steps written, judgements declared, sensitivity run, validity evidence gathered, recognition recorded, card published
why: A score before that is a mashup

rule: Treat the belief that decision-makers prefer a composite as Practice until evidence is found
why: No study found either way; the one commentary read calls the spread "mostly advocacy-driven"

rule: Which form; which construct and parts; who weights; which aggregation and tail; how much of the card on the face; how recognition is gathered; how the audit runs
why: Open choices with named trade-offs

rule: How the card, the sliders, the profile shape and the interval are styled
why: Free within the design system and Chapter 3's rules

rule: Before any behavioural figure is read, name the population the record observes and who it cannot see
why: Revealed-preference methods "only measure use-value"; footfall is one network's 24m devices with residents and workers excluded; card data skews "younger and more metropolitan"
source: Fujiwara & Campbell 2011; ONS RTI methodology 2026; ONS 2016; Wesolowski et al. 2012

rule: Treat distance as a price only with the method's assumptions stated: single purpose, a declared value of time, substitutes considered
why: "If a trip has more than one purpose, it almost certainly violates the travel cost model's central assumption"; time valued at "one-third to the full wage", neither bound firm
source: US EPA 2010; Fujiwara & Campbell 2011; Poor & Smith 2004†

rule: Define a catchment by a self-containment threshold on observed flows, and state the threshold
why: TTWAs: 75% both ways, 66.7% for large areas — the catchment is a rule, not a radius

rule: Measure return as survival with censoring; a visitor who has not yet returned is censored, not lost
why: Simple rates "ignore the duration spent"; censoring "(a) a patient has not (yet) experienced the relevant outcome"

rule: Report diversity as variety, balance and disparity, and declare which the index weights; count supplied and consumed diversity separately
why: "Each is a necessary but insufficient property"; "diversity increases when variety is the sole consideration, whereas taking balance or disparity into account leads to the opposite conclusion"

rule: Any access score names what it leaves out
why: PTAL "does not take into account the destinations you can travel to from each location or the ease of interchange"

rule: Measure welcome with an instrument validated for belonging, re-tested in the scene's own wording, rather than with a proxy
why: Four elements; eight items; confirmed by factor analysis on n = 293 residents of neighbourhoods

rule: When comparing an audience with "the public", state the national yardstick's definition and reference period
why: 91% engage in 12 months when reading counts; response rate 25%

rule: State survival as a cohort figure with its definition, and mark closures provisional for two years
why: "A business is deemed to have survived if it was born in year t … and it is active … in any part of t plus 1"; deaths "not final until the third year"

rule: Name the sense of "resilience" before measuring it: bounce back, absorb, or adapt
why: Three interpretations in one word; the authors favour the third

rule: Any early-warning indicator states its window, its threshold, and its out-of-sample record
why: 24-month window; "the predictive power of even the best of them may be limited"

rule: Grade every proxy for value as validated, reasonably likely, or neither, on the card
why: A surrogate "is expected to predict that clinical benefit"; "In practice, this requirement frequently fails"

rule: Keep a measure that is not the proxy beside the proxy, and watch for them parting
why: The forest "grew excellently in the first generation"

rule: Label every activity figure gross until the deductions are shown; name which of deadweight, displacement, leakage and substitution were applied and from where
why: "Additionality is the extent to which something happens as a result of an intervention that would not have occurred in the absence of the intervention"; "significant care needs to be taken in using default or ready reckoner values"

rule: Ask of any price-based indicator whether it measures a product or a rent
why: "a rent is paid because corn is high"

rule: Show distributional figures weighted beside unweighted, with the weight and its source
why: "Practitioners must present weighted estimates alongside unweighted estimates"

rule: Never place a social-return ratio in a league table; show it with its story
why: "it is not appropriate to compare the social return ratios alone"

rule: Keep economic displacement (a deduction) and residential displacement (people moved out) apart; show who left, and call it displacement only with the comparison the literature requires and the three readings named
why: Proxies "cannot be relied upon to distinguish between involuntary displacement, voluntary outmigration or incumbent socio-economic uplift"

rule: Label every claim of cause with the rung its evidence reaches; from observational data alone the verbs are "alongside", "after" and "where"; "contributed to" only with a theory of change whose alternatives have been tested
why: "Interventional questions cannot be answered from purely observational information"; "Ruling out of alternative causes in order to claim impact"

rule: Where the question behind a chart is causal, state the question and the rung rather than letting "associated with" stand in for an answer
why: The euphemism hides the question (reconstructed abstract)

rule: Where a causal reading is wanted, show Hill's viewpoints the data can show — gradient, consistency, sequence — and the alternatives considered
why: "is there any other way of explaining the set of facts before us"

rule: A theory-of-change claim names its alternative explanations and the evidence against each
why: "Ruling out of alternative causes in order to claim impact"; a story "stronger and more credible", never "foolproof"

rule: "Leading" is shown only when a lead has been measured against a named reference series; until then two series are two series
why: "it is only Granger causality"; a CLI is built by turning-point comparison

rule: The studio's claim ladder puts the observed fact on top, the anchor claim beneath it marked as contribution, a deadweight line marked as stated preference, and counter-flows
why: Version 1's form, amended by Pearl, Hill and the Additionality Guide

rule: Treat every dashboard view as exploratory; a pattern is a hypothesis with a date until tested outside the data that produced it
why: "the same data cannot be used to generate and test a hypothesis"; holdouts "wear out"
source: COS; Goodfellow et al. 2016; Google MLCC

rule: Judge the surprise of a found comparison against the number of comparisons the view allowed
why: "multiple comparisons can be a problem, even when there is no 'fishing expedition'"

rule: Choose family-wise or false-discovery control for any highlighting rule, and say which
why: The two error rates; neither makes every highlight real

rule: No "significant" badge standing alone as the reason for a highlight or a decision; an error-controlled highlighting rule is not a badge
why: "decisions should not be based only on whether a p-value passes a specific threshold"; "the glitter of the t table"

rule: Treat two trending series as one comparison; do not report their correlation as a finding
why: "sequential years are not independent of each other"
kind: Evidence (Yule by citation; Vigen as plain statement)

rule: Any model on the display states what it is importantly wrong about, which culture it was built in, and the date and population of its last validation
why: "the scientist must be alert to what is importantly wrong"; "population distributions are nonstationary"

rule: A pattern becomes a canonical truth by two tests, out-of-sample and the agreement of the competent; the described are among the competent
why: "Validation literally means to make valid, through the agreement of those judged competent"; KDD step one is "from the customer's viewpoint"
kind: Evidence + Standard for the two tests; Nightlife Culture for who is competent
source: Glover 2014; AQuA Book 2025; Fayyad et al. 1996; Chapter 5 (Sen)

rule: Never read two points as a trend; show a measure against its own history with limits the data set
why: "tells you nothing about trends and how much the data varies naturally"; "You don't set the limits"

rule: Distinguish common-cause from special-cause variation on the face, and say which action each calls for
why: "wild goose chases"

rule: Every alert states its false-alarm rate and its detection delay, worked out for the measure's own distribution and agreed with the people who answer it
why: ARL ≈ 371 for one rule of a correct 3σ chart on a long stable series; run-length "between seven and nine … you should decide"

rule: Judge an anomaly against the same season in previous years, not the previous period
why: "data from the less recent past often encompass relevant information about e.g., seasonality"

rule: Surveillance claims state their comparator and their boundary
why: "could have indicated an 'alarm' … depending on the data source and the comparator"

rule: Never rank places of different sizes by a raw rate; show the interval or do not rank
why: "Small schools are overrepresented at both tails, exactly as expected"

rule: Define "small" by precision needed, not by geography
why: "the sample size is not large enough for a direct design-based estimation of sufficient precision"

rule: Show the direct figure with its interval and the shrunk figure with its weight, side by side; mark modelled figures modelled with their covariates named; label a complete count's interval as drawn from its history, a sample's from its sampling
why: Weight on the model = sampling variance ÷ total variance; two observations gave "an implausibly high estimate"

rule: No trend arrow on a modelled small-area figure
why: Its intervals "should not be used to measure change"

rule: Say whether a withheld figure is withheld for confidentiality or for precision, and never let the same mark mean both
why: NHS 1–7 as "*"; Analysis Function 2/3/5; OPN base > 10; ASHE's dark green means both
source: NHS England 2023; Analysis Function 2026; ONS OPN 2025; ONS ASHE 2018

rule: Set the identifying threshold by the scene's knowability, above the national rule where local knowledge would name the units
why: The national rules assume an intruder without local knowledge

rule: Record the ten-line claim record beneath every statement of value; "not done" is written, not hidden
why: A visible boundary is a boundary; a hidden one is an overclaim
kind: Nightlife Culture (with Standard behind each line)

rule: Every comparison carries the comparison record: what is held equal, who chose the comparators, the standardisation, the order, the interval, the season, the base month, the design, the ripple, the future's terms; a line that cannot be filled says "not done"
why: A comparison is a claim that two things are alike in all but one respect; the claim is shown or it is assumed
kind: Standard behind each line; Nightlife Culture for the record as a whole

rule: No league table of places on any measure, and no bands of position (quintiles and the like); position is shown within a distribution with its interval, in categories of statistical separation from an expectation if categories are needed
why: Rankings "play a crucial role in creating this hierarchy"; "about two thirds of all possible comparisons do not allow separation"; "Remove the aggregate index and country rankings"; ranks of many small units do not survive their intervals
kind: Evidence + Standard; the extension to every measure on a dashboard of small places is a Reading
source: Espeland & Sauder†; Goldstein & Spiegelhalter 1996; Marshall & Spiegelhalter 1998; Mogstad et al.†; EPR 2021; SHMI; RSS 2005†

rule: Where a single place's rank must be stated (a reader asks "where do we stand?"), it is given as a range, and a small unit's rank on a rate is not stated at all
why: "ranks are extremely unreliable statistical summaries … particularly for smaller institutions"; about one city in five has a rank interval of ±3 or more under modelling choices alone
source: Marshall & Spiegelhalter; JRC C3 2017/2019; Chapter 5; Chapter 6

rule: Compare places on a funnel or against a declared expectation, never by sorted value alone; where a display is sorted, the sort is a reading aid and the finding is position against limits
why: "avoid spurious ranking of institutions into 'league tables'"; "Always rank bars by value" is a readability rule

rule: State and handle over-dispersion before reading points outside a funnel
why: "could lead to a large number of institutions being inappropriately classified as 'abnormal'"

rule: Standardise for the drivers of a rate before comparing places, or state that the rate is crude and why
why: Equal crude rates in populations of different structure mean unequal performance

rule: An observed-to-expected ratio is compared with the expectation, and with other ratios only under the two conditions the method names; it is not ranked
why: "should only be directly compared to each other if the age structures … are similar to the standard, or if the ratio of their age-specific … rates to that of the standard is consistent across the age groups"; "It is inappropriate to rank trusts according to their SHMI"

rule: Peers are chosen by a published method with a stated distance, a fixed number appropriate to the field, and a stated assumption, applied to every place alike before any comparison; each carries a label for how like it is
why: ONS 20 by Euclidean distance; DfE 10 with closeness bands; "It was assumed that local authorities with similar characteristics would perform or progress at a similar rate"

rule: Self-chosen comparators are shown beside the published set, labelled as chosen, and the choice is kept as data; they never define the comparison alone
why: "peer groups are constructed in a manner that biases compensation upward, particularly in firms outside the … S&P 500"; "Preliminary evidence suggests that increased disclosure has reduced the biases"
source: Faulkender & Yang 2010†; Bizjak et al. 2011†; version 1 Ch 5

rule: Where each of two places exceeds the other on different measures, say they cannot be ordered
why: "The evidence of conflicts is smashed out by aggregation methods to obtain a single quantity, which allows a ranking"

rule: Identity measures — those the studio designates nominal, and says so — are never on an ordered axis; condition measures are compared through the gate, which now includes interval, standardisation and order
why: Version 1's split, extended and its examples corrected by this chapter

rule: Name every trend line's method and window; show no end-point of a trend-cycle without a warning
why: "The smoothness of the trend-cycle can also be controlled by the user"; "the most recent values should not be shown because of the end-point problem"

rule: Mark seasonally adjusted figures as estimates subject to revision, name the method, and adjust no series under three years
why: "seasonal factors are estimates based on present and past experience"; "just one additional observation results in revisions … for several years"; "Very short series (less than 3 years) cannot be seasonally adjusted"

rule: Do not seasonally adjust a series that is not seasonal
why: "will often introduce an artificial seasonal element"

rule: A year-on-year figure shows both ends; a period-on-period figure uses the adjusted series; the display says which growth rate it leads with and why
why: "does not completely remove all seasonal effects"; the base effect; "Monthly growth should therefore be used with caution and alongside other measures"
source: ABS; Eurostat §7.2; ECB 2007; ONS retail bulletin

rule: Percentage points are not per cent; index points are not per cent; cash is not volume; an index names its base
why: "A fall of 1% would result in a value of 9.9%"; "index value changes are affected by the level of the index in relation to its base period"; "value data are deflated to produce … volume measures"
source: ONS style guide; BLS; ONS RSI QMI; HMT deflators guide

rule: Before any change in a place selected for being extreme is read, regression to the mean is named as the first explanation
why: "should always be considered as a possible cause of an observed change"; "Even if subjects are not treated the mean … will go down"

rule: Every series carries its breaks and its revision status; a consistent back series is provided or its absence stated
why: "Explain the nature and extent of the change, and provide a consistent back series where possible"
source: Code of Practice 3.0 §7.5, §3.9; ONS revisions policy

rule: Describe a change by direction, absolute size and relative size; call a change within random variation indicative, not definitive; never caveat with "care must be taken" alone
why: The Analysis Function's own rules

rule: Do not use "significant" of a change unless making a point about statistical significance
why: ONS style

rule: No fixed number of observations is claimed as enough for a trend; the series' length and noise are stated and what they support
why: "These are misleading and unsubstantiated in theory or practice"

rule: A before-and-after display lists its eight rivals and uses no verb stronger than "after"; an interrupted series with its impact model declared may say "departed from its trend"
why: Design 2 is "a 'bad example'"; history, maturation, testing, instrumentation, regression, selection, mortality, interaction
kind: Evidence; the verbs are a Nightlife Culture reading

rule: An interrupted-series claim records its impact model before the after-data are examined, lists co-interventions, handles season and autocorrelation, and carries a control where one exists
why: "the essential, yet often omitted, step of proposing the impact model a priori"; "cannot exclude confounding due to co-interventions"
source: Bernal et al. 2017; Lopez Bernal et al. 2018; Magenta Annex A

rule: A difference-in-differences claim names its comparison group, shows its pre-trend check as a check and not a proof, and reports effects by adoption group when adoption is staggered
why: "cannot be tested because it involves a non-existent counterfactual"; "'Passing' these tests does not mean that parallel trends is true"; already-treated units "can serve as controls"
source: Cunningham; Huntington-Klein; Roth 2022; Goodman-Bacon 2021; Callaway & Sant'Anna

rule: A synthetic-control claim shows its weights, its pre-period fit, and its placebos in time and in space, and checks the six contextual requirements and the pre-period
why: "preclude extrapolation"; "make explicit the contribution of each comparison unit"; "small effects will be indistinguishable from other shocks"

rule: A cut-off claim speaks for those near the cut-off, and a matched claim for what was recorded
why: "local average treatment effect"; "only as good as the characteristics used for matching"
source: Magenta Annex A; Lee & Lemieux 2010; DIME

rule: Every intervention claim states whether spillover and displacement were considered, and whether the comparison place was reached by the ripple
why: "Assuming that such spillover effects do not exist is a strong restriction"; "tells us very little if that activity is simply displaced from elsewhere"
source: Magenta Book 2026 §2.3.2; Abadie 2021; What Works Growth

rule: Before an effect is called absent, the minimum detectable effect for the series and the number of places is stated, by a power calculation whose inputs are declared
why: "the effect size below which we may not be able to distinguish that the effect is different from zero, even if it is"; "Sample sizes are too small"

rule: Every intervention claim states its rung on the What Works scale, with any other ladder's differing placement beside it, and the verb that rung earns; plain before/after and place-against-place are the bottom
why: "We define SMS 3 methods to be the minimum standard"; "No comparator" scores zero; "it will not evidence direct causality"
source: What Works Growth SMS; EEF 2019; Nesta 2013

rule: A projection is labelled a projection, states its assumptions first, gives a central estimate with a range, states its switching value, and has been adjusted for optimism bias by the maker's own record or the generic uplift
why: "Projections are not forecasts"; "Practitioners must account for optimism bias"; "A switching value is the value that a key variable would need to change to such that an option stops representing value for money"
source: ONS NPP 2025; Green Book 2026; HMT optimism-bias guidance

rule: Scenarios say what they do not cover, and a single future figure is not shown; the default is an even number of scenarios, taken from the cross-government toolkit over the Bank's baseline-plus-two
why: "Try to include an even number of scenarios"; "Presenting a single figure is best avoided"; "neither all-encompassing nor do they reflect the full distribution of risks"
tier: **Fixed** (no single figure; say what is omitted); **Fixed** as a stance (even number)
source: Uncertainty Toolkit; Bank of England 2026; Futures Toolkit

rule: Keep and show the record of projections against outturn
why: "examines how our forecasts compare to subsequent outturn data"; the Green Book's own-record adjustment

rule: Words for likelihood carry their numbers in the sentence; no verbal likelihood term stands without one
why: "substantially improved only when numerical guidelines are bracketed in text"; "only a small decrease in trust … mostly for verbal uncertainty communication"
source: Wintle et al. 2019; van der Bles et al. 2020†; IPCC 2010

rule: A fast or nowcast series is labelled an early sighting of the present, never a forecast
why: "predicting the present"; "none should be used to predict GDP on their own"
source: Choi & Varian; ONS Data Science Campus; Lazer et al.†

rule: "Leading" is used only of a series with a measured record of turning points against a named reference series — the Conference Board's tests of conformity and consistent timing, or an equivalent stated one — and the record's real-time weakness is noted
why: "Historically, the cyclical turning points in the leading index have occurred before"; "rarely provided adequate signals" in real time

rule: A borrowed concentration threshold names its jurisdiction; a churn figure publishes its recipe; an average over survivors says who left
why: HHI thresholds are American and the CMA applies none; no official churn; survivorship

rule: Every dashboard that intends to be read next year carries, published beside it, the service record: freshness promise, dependencies, refresh, watch and alarm, availability and degraded mode, budget and device, map supply, retirement, owner, not-done
why: A dashboard is "a digital service" to be "continually" managed; the promise its first screen makes has to be kept by something
kind: Standard + Nightlife Culture for the record as a whole

rule: Each series states the period it describes, the date published, the date last revised and its declared frequency; "last updated" alone is never shown
why: "Always make it clear which dates or period"; the catalogue standards separate the dates and the frequency; a date without a frequency does not say whether the figure is late; an absent date means one of three things
kind: Standard (the period); Nightlife Culture (the four parts)
source: Analysis Function 2026; DCAT 3; DCAT-AP 3; DCMI; ONS revisions policy

rule: The page's freshness lifetime is declared in days, compared against the data's date on the page itself, and shown in words a reader can read
why: "A 'stale' response is one where" its age has exceeded its lifetime; "The oldest data is no older than Y" is a checkable sentence

rule: A change to the data carries a change note saying what changed and when; the page is never marked updated without saying what
why: "Do not say the page has been updated without saying what has changed"

rule: Revisions and corrections are distinguished and dated; a figure open to revision says until when
why: "A revision is a scheduled change"; "A correction is an unplanned revision … because of the identification of an error"
source: ONS revisions policy; Code of Practice 3.0 §3.9

rule: Every dependency is recorded with its stated limit, its terms, the notice it has promised, and the date its page was read; it is marked as needed at build time or at read time, and as a dependency on *supply* or on *terms*
why: The open licence "does not guarantee the continued supply"; the platform terms address storing, deriving, combining and scheduled calling clause by clause

rule: The stated rate limit is the real limit; the refresh job never relies on capacity beyond it, respects `Retry-After`, keeps a clock per interface, and backs off with jitter
why: "you should not let your users go over the limits you set even if you have spare capacity"; "Always use randomized exponential backoff"
source: GDS service levels; RFC 6585; ONS bots; SRE ch. 22

rule: A beta-labelled or no-service-level interface is treated as able to change without notice, whatever its publisher
why: "there may occasionally be breaking changes"; beta "where your users are expecting breaking changes" need not be given the six months
source: ONS developer hub; GDS live API guidance

rule: Response headers announcing deprecation and sunset are read by the refresh job and raise a ticket
why: The statistics office signals retirement by `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link` headers, then 404; a client reading only the body cannot see it coming
tier: Adaptable (which interfaces signal); **Fixed** (that the job reads them)

rule: Platform interfaces are used only within their written terms; a series derived from a platform whose terms forbid deriving it is not built
why: III.13: "Do not analyze … creating new or derived listenership metrics"; "non-commercial use only"
source: Spotify Developer Policy; Skiddle; Last.fm; Ticketmaster

rule: Whether to call a platform at all is a recorded decision made with its terms open, not a default
why: A dependency on terms is theirs to withdraw

rule: Fetch at build time, not at read time; the reader's page depends on its host alone, and every other dependency is the night's job's
why: "A service cannot be more available than the intersection of all its critical dependencies"; ten at 99.9% is 3.65 days a year
tier: **Fixed** as a stance; Adaptable for a declared live element
source: Treynor et al. 2017; SRE availability table; Willison 2021

rule: On a failed fetch the last good copy is kept and shown with its age; the page is never blanked
why: "Invalidating or emptying local state as a result of a failed refresh" is a named anti-pattern; `stale-if-error`; "Stale data is almost always better than incorrect data"

rule: Each series is its own compartment; a closed source empties one panel and not the page
why: "if one element fails, the others continue to function"; "Integration points are the number-one killer of systems"

rule: The degraded mode is exercised before launch and on a schedule, and the date recorded
why: "the code path you never use is the code path that (often) doesn't work"

rule: The availability objective is set in the data's terms, written before launch, and not higher than readers can tell
why: "100% is the wrong reliability target"; "Users build on the reality of what you offer, rather than what you say you'll supply"
tier: **Fixed** as a stance; Adaptable in value

rule: A page that loads with the wrong or stale content is counted as an error, so the watch checks the data's date and not the status code
why: Errors include "an HTTP 200 success response, but coupled with the wrong content"

rule: The watch is independent of the job and the scheduler, pinged by the job after the effect is confirmed, recorded as a dependency in its own right, and its ticket goes to a role with a named second
why: Schedules are delayed, "may be dropped", are disabled after 60 quiet days and notify "the user who last modified the cron syntax"; "monitoring of the effect of cron jobs"

rule: Signals are sorted into alerts, tickets and logs; a failed refresh is a ticket; the one alert is the page lying about its date
why: "Every page should be actionable" (a page being a pager alert); "humans should be notified only when they need to take action"

rule: The refresh job is idempotent and, in doubt, skipped rather than doubled; scheduled off the hour
why: "we favor skipping launches rather than risking double launches"; "High load times include the start of every hour"
source: SRE ch. 24; SRE workbook; GitHub docs

rule: Every fetch is committed to a version history so that any figure's vintage is recoverable by date
why: "records changes to that resource over time in the commit history"; a living series owes its archive

rule: The free tier's limits are recorded in the service record as design constraints with a date, and no availability is assumed of it
why: 25 MiB per asset; 1 GB per site; paused at the credit cap; no commitment could be established

rule: The cost of a live element is computed with the studio's own expected numbers before it is chosen
why: Billing is per initialisation; "A map load is counted every time Mapbox GL JS initializes"

rule: The page is budgeted for the seventy-fifth-percentile phone and network, not the builder's, and tested on one
why: "15-25% as fast as those carried by programmers and their bosses"; "a good threshold to measure is the 75th percentile"
kind: Practice (a reasoned model) + Evidence (the Almanac's medians)

rule: Figures and the table are in the HTML and shown before any script runs; the page is not a single-page application
why: "Government services should be functional using only HTML" (a standard for government services, adopted here); "1.1% of people aren't getting JavaScript enhancements (1 in 93)", four-fifths involuntarily

rule: Total weight is held within Russell's five-second budget for the baseline phone — about 1.3 MiB with half script, 2.5 MiB with almost none — and the vector renderer is counted against the script line before it is chosen
why: "650KiB of JavaScript" or "100KiB of JavaScript" at five seconds; the renderer is about 287 KB gzipped
tier: **Fixed** as a stance; Adaptable in figure

rule: The "53% abandon" figure is not used without its date, source and wording, and preferably not at all
why: Vendor research, 2016, n=3.7K opt-in sites, "likely to be abandoned"

rule: The map's tile supply is one of four named kinds, recorded with what was agreed to: cache, attribution, logo, offline, non-commercial, pause
why: "Our tile servers are not [free]"; "no SLA or guarantee"; "service will pause"; "Offline use is not permitted"

rule: Boundary files are the generalised product appropriate to the scale, cut to the area shown, with their date and two-owner attribution; a boundary vintage is pinned and stated
why: BFC about 128 MB against BSC about 1.7 MB in the same record; "as at December 2024"; "Contains both Ordnance Survey and ONS Intellectual Property Rights"
source: ONS digital boundaries; Open Geography Portal; Decision Book DTA-05/06

rule: Simplification is checked for vanished small polygons before publication
why: "At high simplification, small polygons can disappear entirely"

rule: Every map has a non-map twin — the same figures by the same places as a table — reachable before the script; pan and zoom have buttons; the sequential ramp is short
why: "make sure the data is available in another format such as a downloadable data table"; WCAG 2.5.1 and 2.5.7 examples; five blues
source: Analysis Function colours; WCAG 2.2; WAI complex images

rule: The notice the studio gives when retiring a series, and the archive address, are written before the first series needs them; a retired series stays reachable
why: "Do this at least six months before retirement"; "keeping data and metadata available, with a clear note that it is no longer updated"; "This publication was withdrawn on"
tier: **Fixed** as a procedure; Adaptable in period
source: Analysis Function 2026; GOV.UK withdrawal; Code of Practice 3.0 §10.7

rule: The owner of the ticket is a role with a successor, and the record says where it lives
why: "not an appropriate project for a single person"; 65% of projects at truck factor ≤ 2

rule: The record's last line states what the dashboard does not promise
why: "Users build on the reality of what you offer, rather than what you say you'll supply"

rule: Every felt measure carries the measure record: construct and register, items, who chose, who was asked, who answered, the spread, the five sources of validity evidence, recognition, discordance, what this changed
why: A measure is validated by accumulated evidence for a use; without the record nothing accumulates
kind: Standard + Nightlife Culture for the record as a whole

rule: The construct is named in words, and its register (made / perceived / excess), before any item is written; the three registers are never collapsed into one number
why: "define the construct before the proxy"; a "fuzzy concept … flourishes precisely because of its imprecision"; no literature proposes a blended score

rule: A measure says whether it is reflective or formative and is validated accordingly
why: "few studies use formative indicator measurement models, even though they should"; the two are misspecified for each other

rule: A felt result is reported as a distribution with bands, never as a point alone; coordinates or scores are computed per respondent, not from the room's median
why: "relying only on average ratings might mask important differences"; "percent of people likely to perceive"

rule: Bands' cut-points are chosen by a stated method — the respondents' own turning point, or an adopted official set — and the method is on the record
why: "the mid-point of the scale (5) acts as an important cut-off for respondents"
tier: **Fixed** as a procedure; Adaptable in value

rule: A borrowed attribute word is checked for how it is read before it is used; "vibrant" in particular is a derived diagonal and the least evenly read axis of the standard instrument
why: "a general non-equidistant interpretation of the scales, particularly on the vibrant-monotonous direction"

rule: The place is defined to the respondent in the question, at a stated scale
why: "By neighbourhood we mean a few minutes walking distance from your home"

rule: In situ and retrospective answers are different measures (experienced; evaluative) and are not pooled or compared as one
why: Experienced wellbeing "is concerned with people's emotional states"; evaluative "refers to judgments"

rule: Every felt measure states its recruitment route, response, known gaps and the share contributed by its most active contributors
why: "Mapping effort was highest in sampling groups whose livelihoods were closely related to the purpose"; "90-9-1"; "those who choose to participate are frequently quite unrepresentative"

rule: The ceiling is named: a felt measure taken only among those present is a measure of those who chose to be there
why: "relatively low variance and high scores observed on attachment"

rule: No felt estimate is published below the official floor (fewer than 50 answers or a numerator under 5), and its precision band is stated
why: "not published if the sample size they are based on is fewer than 50"; CV bands

rule: A felt measure for a place is compared with its own history or with declared peers, and Chapter 7's rule against ranking applies
why: "progress over time within the same local authority, or across local authorities that share a similar demographic composition"

rule: Self-placement used as a measure is private before it is public, is one item among several, and its visible form is labelled a conversation, not a measure
why: "even mild social influence can undermine the wisdom of crowd effect"; a single item of a non-concrete construct; the living histogram's artefact
source: Lorenz et al. 2011 †; Diamantopoulos et al. 2012; Schilling et al. 2002

rule: An open, repeatable vote is never presented as a measure of the place
why: "Boaty McBoatface topped the list with over 124,000 votes"; "this is an Internet poll"

rule: Where representativeness is claimed, recruitment is by sample first; where it is not, the claim is bounded to the participants
why: "Randomly selecting participants from among the general population is the best guarantee of descriptive representativeness"; "We make no claim that the maps produced represent a coherent and fixed" community
source: Fung 2006; Deliberative Democracy Lab; Reed et al. 2025

rule: A story-of-change method is used for the significant, not the average, and is not relied on as the accountability case
why: its own manual lists "understand the average experience of participants" and accountability reporting among the things other methods do more efficiently

rule: "What this changed" is a line on every felt measure: how many answered, what they said, how it informed the decision, within a stated time, told to the people who answered
why: "Explain the responses that have been received from consultees and how these have informed the policy"; responsiveness "associated with a 57 percent increase" in taking part again
source: Cabinet Office 2018; Sjoberg et al. 2017 †; Arnstein 1969

rule: Report-back is tailored to those who answered, not generic
why: "the tailored newsletter, or sending no newsletter at all, were equally effective … and significantly better than the general newsletter"

rule: "Co-produced" is used only where the people who gave the data share in what is done with it; otherwise "participatory"
why: "Co-design and other forms of asking the advice of users … can lack any continuing involvement in delivery"

rule: Co-presence is shown as *who was there together*; it is called a tie only after the co-occurrence count has been tested against opportunity, and centrality computed from co-presence is not shown as a measure of anyone's importance
why: "not easily usable to build in a reliable and systematic fashion surrogate contact data"; "whether an observed number of co-occurrences … is significant"; baseline v inbreeding homophily
source: Génois & Barrat 2018; Neal et al. 2021; McPherson et al. 2001

rule: A two-mode network states its boundary — which events and people are in it — because omitting contexts inflates clustering
why: "network boundary specification and fixed choice designs can dramatically alter estimates of network-level statistics"

rule: Return is shown as return; stated intention to return is not a measure of it, and return alone is not attachment
why: "no statistically significant correlation exists between intention and actual repeat visitation rates"; loyalty is attitude *and* patronage

rule: An amenity or premises count is labelled an indicator coded by outsiders, never a descriptor
why: "Can what are in the end organizational directories really get at … the experiential meaning of place?"; "availability does not necessarily mean access"
source: Silver, Clark & Navarro 2010; Rhubart et al. 2022

rule: A trace is labelled for the population it records and used within-sample; its skew is stated
why: "Nonrepresentative data are bad for out-of-sample generalizations, but can be quite useful for within-sample comparisons"; "24.4 times the number of Foursquare users per capita"
source: Salganik; Hecht & Stephens 2014; Malik et al. 2015; Chapter 4

rule: A trace or signal is shown as an indicator of a vibe only after it has been validated against a descriptor in the place and population concerned; until then it is labelled an unvalidated indicator
why: 77% of an "assumed" proxy; dictionaries "inconsistent"; a signal that flipped sign; "related but distinct constructs"
source: De Nadai et al. 2016; Jaidka et al. 2020 (reconstructed); Brown & Coyne 2018; Orstad et al. 2017 †

rule: Text sentiment is labelled as "how people appear to others", with its platform's reach and the tools' known error by speaker stated
why: "we quantify only how people appear to others"; parser recall "64.0%" against "80.4%"
source: Dodds et al. 2011; Blodgett et al. 2016

rule: No inference of feeling from faces is built, and none from gait or voice without the evidence the face lacks
why: "no unique mapping between a configuration of facial movements and instances of an emotion category"; the field's own ethics sheet on "utterance, facial expression, gait, etc."; Article 5(1)(f) for biometric inference at work and in education

rule: Crowdsourced perception of images is labelled as the judgement of the raters, with who they were
why: "76.0% identified themselves as male"; predicts "human judgments of pairwise image comparisons"
source: Salesses et al. 2013; Dubey et al. 2016

rule: A sound measure uses what is heard and by whom before how loud; a song-feature proxy is labelled defined-not-derived and supply-withdrawn
why: the review's report of Axelsson et al.: "perceived sound sources are more important as indicators … than sound levels"; valence defined, derivation unpublished; endpoint withdrawn Nov 2024
source: Aletta, Kang & Axelsson 2016; Spotify reference; Chapter 8

rule: Experience sampling, where used, is within-person, its sample described, and its respondents' burden counted as a cost
why: "using only the within-individual variation"; "all Apple iOS users"; "difficult to scale up"
source: MacKerron & Mourato 2013 †; Seresinhe et al. 2019; NRC 2013

rule: A new felt item is cognitively tested before it is asked, placed with known context effects, and administered in a stated mode
why: "Cognitive testing was undertaken to understand how respondents chose their score"; "strongly affected by question structure and context"; mode effects

rule: Validity is claimed for an interpretation and a use, argued from the five sources; the record says which have evidence and which say "not yet"
why: "It is the interpretations of test scores for proposed uses that are evaluated, not the test itself"

rule: Recognition is gathered as member checking — who was shown what, what they said, what changed — and recorded as content and response-process evidence plus legitimacy; it is never presented as validation complete
why: "Face validity is at best a very weak kind of evidence"; member checking "often mentioned as one in a list"
source: Price et al. 2015; Birt et al. 2016 †; Chapter 5

rule: Reliability is reported where measured and marked "not yet" where not; a 0.70 floor is named as the common minimum and 0.90 as the recommended one
why: "a reliability coefficient of 0.70 has often been accepted as satisfactory"; "0.90 is the minimum recommended threshold"

rule: Felt and counted layers are integrated by a declared protocol with four cells — agreement, partial agreement, silence, dissonance — and discordance is reported, not resolved by preferring the number
why: "Discordance occurs if …"; "the only one to include silence"
source: Fetters, Curry & Creswell 2013; O'Cathain, Murphy & Nicholl 2010

rule: The discordant cell is pre-committed before the dashboard is built
why: Pre-registration of the integration; version 1's rule

rule: The measure's effect on the measured is gathered as consequences evidence after launch, including the extraction question
why: Consequences are a source of validity evidence; "the mix and balance of extraction and empowerment"

rule: Every dashboard that shows people carries the safeguards record: what is held and about whom, the basis, the release model, the method per view, the query-time controls, the walk, who was consulted, who governs and who stood at the door, the held layer, withdrawal, harm, regimes, moderation, review and what this changed
why: Anonymisation "is a process of risk management but it is also a dynamic decision-making process"; the statute requires "appropriate safeguards"
kind: Standard (law) + Practice + Nightlife Culture for the record as a whole
source: UK GDPR Art 84B; Elliot, Mackey & O'Hara; this chapter §19

rule: The first line of the record is written before the first row is collected, is dated, and names a person
why: By design and by default; the regulator's step 1
source: UK GDPR Art 25; ICO DPIA steps

rule: Anonymity is assessed in the data environment — what else is public, who is motivated, what tools exist — and reassessed on a stated schedule
why: "not a property of the data"; "periodically review the decisions you take"
source: Elliot, Mackey & O'Hara; ICO anonymisation guidance

rule: The identifiability test is the motivated intruder, and for a scene the intruder is modelled as a regular with local knowledge
why: "reasonably competent"; "curiosity (eg a local person's desire …)"; "one person or group knows a great deal about another person"

rule: The disclosure floor is set per view, above the national rule where the scene can name the units, and stated; its value is a judgement scaled to sensitivity
why: "make a judgement call for other low counts, depending on the sensitivity"; online tools "stricter"; "A minimum cell count equal to five is suggested"
tier: **Fixed** as a procedure; Adaptable in value
source: ONS births and deaths policy §4.2.2, §4.4; Chapter 6

rule: The precision floor and the disclosure floor are two numbers for two objects, both stated; a count above the disclosure floor whose mean is below the precision floor is shown as a count, not a score
why: Fifty is a reliability rule; two, three, five and seven are identification rules
source: ONS QMI; ONS births and deaths policy; this chapter §5

rule: Suppression is primary and secondary, across every linked view; or a consistent cell key is used so the same cell shows the same way everywhere; the choice is declared
why: "additional cells will have to be suppressed (secondary suppression)"; "If a cell requires protection in one table then it will require protection in all tables"; "the same cell value and cell key"
source: ONS policy; Handbook on SDC; ONS Census 2021 methodology

rule: Every floor is paired with a form that keeps the small present — a band, a presence mark, a held status — and a withheld cell is marked, never blank
why: "suppression rules disproportionately impact small population groups and small areas"; "Missing data is not the same as a zero value"; the brief's "aggregation of 'the biggest'"
source: Abowd & Hawes; UKSA geospatial ethics; Chapter 4; the brief

rule: A rate or share whose underlying counts are small is treated as disclosive even if the counts are not published
why: "A rate or other statistic may be disclosive if it is possible to infer that the underlying counts contain small numbers"

rule: Classifications readers may filter by are fixed; a reader-drawn boundary, reader-defined category or free time window is treated as a table builder and protected as one
why: "a set of standard classifications"; differencing "two or more overlapping tables and subtraction"; variable caps
source: ONS policy; ONS Census 2021 table builder

rule: An interactive view is protected as an online tool: either a limit on overlapping views with a request log (per user where readers register, per session where they do not) audited by a named person, or a consistent cell key with capped combinations; registration for deeper views where the studio chooses; controls "kept under review"
why: "generate multiple tables and potentially to attempt to breach confidentiality"; registration, log, "If possible, … a limit on the number of similar tables"
tier: **Fixed** as a procedure; Adaptable in parts

rule: Before release and at each data release, a friendly intruder who knows the scene walks the views for a bounded time; claims and confidences are recorded; a small number of low-confidence correct claims is the standard, not zero
why: "friendly intruders"; "around a half day"; "Each identification claim is given a percentage of confidence"; "a small number of correct claims with low confidence"
source: ONS intruder testing; version 1's filter walk

rule: Hiding one field is not relied on as protection against repeated queries; the walk tests chosen positions, not single views
why: Trilateration succeeded with distance hidden: "up to the victim's building"

rule: Differential privacy, if used, is used for what it protects — a person's participation — and never presented as protecting a group; its budget and its small-area cost are published
why: "It is the conclusions reached in the study that affect the smoker"; (kε, 0) for groups of size k; "systematically undercounts … mixed-race"; "aggregate small populations"
source: Dwork & Roth; Kenny et al.; US Census Bureau

rule: Synthetic data is for demonstration, test and download, never the face, and is released only where no "real or perceived risk of disclosure" remains
why: "it is not acceptable to release a synthetic dataset that could lead to a real or perceived risk of disclosure"

rule: Pseudonymised rows are treated as personal data; a hash is not anonymisation
why: "Pseudonymised personal data remains personal data"; "computing the 22M hashes took less than 2 minutes"

rule: Every statutory citation in the record carries the date read and the version; the record is re-read against the current text on a stated schedule
why: Article 89 and s.19 omitted 5 February 2026; the regulator renamed 30 September 2026; guidance "under review"
