rule: A lawful basis is recorded per purpose before collection; the house does not use consent as the basis for anything it will publish, taking as its reason the regulator's sentence on research — a stance, since the regulator's sentence is narrower and a consent basis with a declared cut-off is the funder's own practice
why: "If you would not be able to fully action a withdrawal of consent … you should not use consent as your lawful basis"; "no exemption to this for scientific research"; Art 8A(4)
source: ICO valid consent; UK GDPR Arts 7(3), 8A(4)

rule: Where legitimate interests is the basis, the three-part test is run and the assessment kept
why: "identify a legitimate interest; show … necessary; and balance it"

rule: Whether the research and statistics provisions fit is a question put to counsel and recorded as open until answered; the two exclusions are checked in terms
why: "substantial damage or substantial distress"; "measures or decisions with respect to a particular data subject"; "aggregate data that is not personal data"

rule: No panel infers a special-category characteristic about the people in a place unless an Article 9 condition, a DPIA and consultation are on the record; an onlooker's likely inference is written into the harm assessment as a fairness question
why: "regardless of how confident you are that the inference is correct"; "other people could (rightly or wrongly) infer"

rule: Data about identifiable people taken from a platform or a public source carries Article 14's notice or a published reason, and the record says where it came from
why: "no automatic exception … just because the personal data is in the public domain"; "must take appropriate measures … including by making the information available publicly"; "lawful reason … even when it is publicly available"

rule: The house does a DPIA for any dashboard that combines sources, re-uses public data, tracks location or behaviour, or profiles — the regulator requires one for the first and, combined with another criterion, for the others; it seeks the views of those affected or their representatives; it is published unless there is a stated reason
why: The regulator's high-risk list; "Where appropriate, the controller shall seek the views of data subjects or their representatives"; "good practice to publish"
source: UK GDPR Art 35; ICO DPIA guidance

rule: The site's own analytics count how the service is used, never who uses it, or run on consent
why: "It is about how your service is used, not about who uses it"; demographic segmentation "cannot rely on the statistical purposes exception"
source: PECR Sch A1 para 5; ICO storage and access guidance

rule: The children's tests are applied and the evidence kept: more probable than not, and who actually uses the service
why: "more probable than not"; "based on evidence about who actually uses a service"
source: ICO Children's Code; UK GDPR Art 25(1A); OSA s.35

rule: A free dashboard is a service to the public under the Equality Act; every map has an accessible twin; a panel's rules are checked for particular disadvantage to a protected group
why: "for payment or not"; "provided in an accessible format"; "a particular disadvantage"

rule: If the public can write what the public sees, the dashboard is run as a regulated service: a named accountable individual, a risk assessment within three months of launch, moderation, reporting and complaints routes, a written record
why: s.3(1); "services of all sizes"; "three months to complete a risk assessment"; the measures for all services

rule: A community is consulted, governs and agrees; it is never asked to consent, and no agreement by a community or its leaders is recorded as a person's consent
why: "should not be mistaken for community consent"; "In no case should a collective community agreement … substitute"

rule: Consultation is tailored to the community and recorded with what it changed; the record names who it was reached through
why: "must be tailored to the communities"; gatekeepers "may also have other interests"

rule: Indigenous data-sovereignty frameworks are cited for their questions and structure and never adopted as the authority for a non-Indigenous community's claim; the house's layer carries the house's name
why: "specifically First Nations—not Indigenous"; "inherent rights to self-determination as sovereign entities"; "a normative foundation"
source: FNIGC; Kukutai & Taylor; Carroll et al.

rule: "Less defined types of consent shall be balanced by stronger governance arrangements": a held layer is at the collaborate or empower level of the spectrum or it is not called community-held
why: "Less defined types of consent shall be balanced by stronger governance arrangements"; the five levels
source: Te Mana Raraunga 5.2; Ada Lovelace Institute

rule: Withdrawal tiers, the cut-off and what cannot be undone are written before the first contribution and told at it
why: "cannot then be excluded"; "it would not be possible to remove data from research that had already taken place"; "as easy to withdraw as to give"
source: ESRC; UK Biobank; UK GDPR Art 7(3)

rule: A withdrawn item leaves a tombstone: identifier kept, content removed, reason stated; copies are not promised back
why: "the reason for the withdrawal will be indicated on a tombstone page"; "You cannot remove sensitive data from other users' clones"

rule: The held layer is a declared status for a category, never a marker on a unit: present in a coarser count, decided by a named process, reason public, review date set, tested by the walk against public lists; it is drawn as held and never as empty
why: eBird, iNaturalist, NBN Atlas; "presumption in favour of disclosure" with a named harm; "Missing data is not the same as a zero value"
kind: Practice + Standard (law, by analogy) + Nightlife Culture
source: eBird; NBN Atlas; EIR 2004 reg 12; UKSA

rule: Holding is a decision and not a default: local and small-area data are not avoided because they carry risk
why: "should not necessarily be used as a rationale for avoiding local or small area data altogether"

rule: The harm assessment has three columns — persons, groups, places — and the place column asks about stigma, speculation, findability and the ecological fallacy for every panel
why: The regulator's list is individual; "blight a geographic area or community"; "stigmatisation"; "a leading indicator for housing price changes"
source: ICO DPIA; UKSA; Aaronson et al.; Glaeser et al. †

rule: No panel grades or ranks places, and where a value is drawn by colour the scale is checked for stigma; a money view is lit for a scene only after its governance has agreed, the speculation reading has been assessed, and both are on the record
why: The lending maps "led to reduced home ownership rates"; "impact on the community over the intentions of the designer"
source: Aaronson et al.; Design Justice Network; Chapter 7

rule: Colour and area are checked for stigma: no red or dark for low, no dominance of large empty areas, and "fewer" never drawn as "nothing"
why: "Red traditionally spells danger"; "Large areas … tend to dominate visually"; "Missing data is not the same as a zero value"

rule: Moderation is designed as verbs and adverbs before contributions open, with gating that prices rather than excludes where it can, and its uneven cost on who contributes is counted in the measure record
why: "excluding, pricing, organizing, and norm-setting"; "seven-in-ten"; "76% … made changes to the way they use the platforms"

rule: The safety burden is designed in, not left to the user
why: "The burden of safety should never fall solely upon the user"

rule: A breach or a failure of protection is stated in public and addressed in public
why: "Be transparent about breaches of privacy and act publicly in addressing weaknesses"

rule: The quotation rule applies to the dashboard as to the book: institutions are quoted; private persons are not identified by it or through it
why: The chapter's own method; the case reached only through a tertiary source

rule: After launch, the record's last line asks who benefited from being made visible and who paid, and answers with evidence
why: "unintended consequences"; "the mix and balance of extraction and empowerment"; consequences as validity evidence

rule: Every view carries a face sheet: the sentence, the pattern and first state, what of each record sits on the face, the nothings, the interactions and their costs, hover and pointer routes, the small-screen form, the state and its address, the snapshot and citation, words, map and colour, tests and review
why: The field describes dashboards and does not evaluate them; the surface must account for itself
source: This chapter §11; Sarikaya et al.; Bach et al.

rule: The first screen's sentence is written before the screen is designed; it answers the named reader's question and works with no interaction
why: Titles are visited first by two-thirds of readers in the one study; a title is remembered over its chart; most readers touch nothing optional
source: Sultanum & Setlur 2026; Kong, Liu & Karahalios 2019; ONS interactive charts; Chapters 1, 3

rule: A dashboard is justified before it is built: a named reader, data updated often enough to revisit, a need for combination, and the resource to maintain it; otherwise charts with specific insights
why: "Only use a dashboard if you have clear justification"; "put the burden of interpreting and understanding data onto the user"

rule: The most important information comes first on every page, section and chart; chart titles state the trend; headings and titles within the official lengths, and within the house's shorter one where it applies
why: Inverted pyramid; "around 28% of content"; "15 words or fewer"; "fewer than 60 characters"; "65 characters or less"
tier: **Fixed**; the house limit Fixed as a stance

rule: The landing pattern is chosen from the six, named in writing, and the exemplar (if any) is declared an endorsement
why: No study compares the patterns; the first-shown view anchors

rule: Nothing is asked of the reader before something is given: no configuration, registration or weighting before the sentence and a figure; a skippable guess offered after the sentence is not a toll
why: "shows the main message without needing any interaction"; a start point gives "just enough information" first; configuration-first taken up by one or two in a hundred
source: ONS; GOV.UK start page; OECD BLI figures

rule: A search or place input sits beside content that already says something, never instead of it
why: Search adopted by two-thirds to four-fifths when offered beside a display; "deeply personal"; no evidence for a blank screen

rule: The small screen is designed first; what is removed for it is recorded as not the message; no hover content is load-bearing
why: "Over half" (ONS) to "Two-thirds" (Analysis Function) arrive on a phone or tablet; "80% … do not scroll past the first quarter"; phone versions "remove content" and "removed the interactivity completely"
source: ONS; Analysis Function; Hoffswell, Li & Liu 2020; Kim, Moritz & Hullman 2021

rule: On a phone, linear layouts and small multiples are the defaults over radial forms and animation
why: 2.8–5.4 s against 3.3–6.9 s; small multiples "consistently completed tasks in less time"

rule: The authored account and exploration are both reachable from the first screen; neither is a toll on the other
why: "The reader is not forced to interact in order to learn"; the taxonomy's commonest structure may open on a default view; the null (secondary)
source: Victor 2011; Segel & Heer 2010; Boy et al. 2015 (secondary)

rule: Every written line links to the view that shows it, and every view to its line
why: Linking "significantly increased user engagement" and improved recall with the slideshow layout

rule: Text on the face is not treated as clutter: the title carries the trend, statistics and context sit by the point, and whatever an annotation carries is also in the text, because annotations may vanish on a phone
why: "heavily annotated charts were not penalized"; "Perceptual content … should be positioned in the title"; "Annotations may not display on mobile devices"
source: Stokes et al. 2023; Ajani et al.; ONS annotations

rule: A title never says what the chart does not show; where they would disagree, the chart is redrawn or the title rewritten
why: Readers recall the title's message and call the result neutral; the chart wins when the caption names a weak feature
source: Kong, Liu & Karahalios 2018, 2019; Kim, Setlur & Agrawala 2021

rule: Generated sentences are built by rule from checked data, their topics ranked per place, checked by a person, labelled as generated, written in the house's voice, and aware of every series break they speak across
why: "not a labour-saving tool"; "all data are checked before publishing"; readability d = 2.8 against; the stock-split error

rule: The "how this argues" page states the display's rhetorical positions — defaults, orderings, denominators, what is held — and is linked from every view; it is written for the reader who checks
why: Four editorial layers; "provenance rhetoric"; "Disclosing some of these decisions is a way to establish trust"; metadata changed thoroughness, not accuracy
source: Hullman & Diakopoulos 2011; Dörk et al. 2013; Burns et al.

rule: Every interaction names its purchase from the table and its costs from the seven, or is cut; the static reading works before it is added
why: "does not improve participants' accuracy … can significantly detract"; a required interaction cut completion and correct choice; seven costs
source: Mosca, Ottley & Chang 2021; Zikmund-Fisher et al. 2011 †; Lam 2008 †; Decision Book Ch 7

rule: Guided tours and onboarding are not relied on to fix a first screen; a familiar form and a sentence are
why: No correctness difference with or without onboarding; readers skim the guide; "only useful once"

rule: Nothing the majority of readers need is one step away; nothing one step away is hidden behind a control readers think will take them off the page; detail on request is two levels at most, with an obvious route
why: "some users avoid clicking the link"; "Do not use the details component to hide information that the majority of your users will need"; "beyond 2 disclosure levels typically have low usability"

rule: Content on hover meets the three conditions (dismissible, hoverable, persistent) and is also reachable by keyboard focus; nothing is only on hover, because touch has no hover
why: SC 1.4.13 and its reasons; "not normally available on touchscreens"; "people using a touchscreen device may not use a physical keyboard"

rule: Every control works by keyboard and by a single pointer without a path or a drag; maps have buttons for zoom and pan
Targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or have an equivalent control that is; dense data marks that must be smaller get an equivalent route — the table twin
why: SC 2.5.8 and its "interactive data visualization where targets are necessarily dense" exception, with "equivalent functionality through alternative means"

rule: A tooltip, where used, repeats what is at the mark or in the table, is spoken and keyboard-reachable, and is never the only place a value lives
why: The ONS's components; the ONS's exemption; no public design system has a tooltip component
source: ONS chart components; ONS interactive charts

rule: Every reachable state has one canonical address that encodes the selection in a fixed order
why: "a URL that links to the current state"; "different parameter settings result in different URLs, and yet provide exactly the same visualization view"; 2,000 characters

rule: Every state can be frozen as a dated, unchanging snapshot of its data and text — at each release at least, and on request or on share — findable from the live view and linking previous, next and live; the citation is generated and carries the address with its selection, the snapshot date, the data version and the retrieval date
why: Links rot; content drifts; "Interactive content usually cannot be archived"; "timeslice, version and/or granular portion"; R1–R14; OWID's archived citations
source: FORCE11 2014; RDA WGDC 2015; Jones et al. 2016; The National Archives; Our World in Data 2025

rule: Data are versioned and timestamped; a correction is announced at the top of the affected view with when and why; a retired view keeps its address under a dated banner; statistics are never silently replaced
why: ONS versions and corrections policy; "Correction of errors are reported at the top of the affected release"; "withdraw the content - this keeps the content on the site"
source: ONS revisions policy; GOV.UK publisher guidance

rule: A cropped or shared copy carries the stamp, the floor note, the unit and the snapshot date
why: The share is the state's afterlife; the data dump is the commonest use
source: Version 1 crop test; Tory et al. 2021

rule: Every view declares the data version, the specification version and the selection it was built from, and a degraded state is a state with an aged data version
why: "independent from the other components"; "unit := (data, transforms, mark-type, encodings)"; "re-evaluated as selections change"

rule: The records' kinds sit on the face as statuses in text that open the record; a source line is followable, not only present
why: Metadata read as "more thorough" without accuracy; a source line "suggests that there may be no need for the user to check"; beauty trusted via inferred competence
source: Burns et al.; Kennedy et al. 2016; Lin & Thornton †; Chapter 4

rule: A cell not shown is marked, explained by kind, and never blank; nothing is imputed into a withheld cell; a series is never joined across a gap; the maker expects, and does not design away, the lower confidence a shown gap produces against a dropped one
why: Dropping the gap was the most biased and the most confident; an explained empty cell beat a blurred one for confidence and raised risk-taking; "Do not join the points"
source: Sarma et al. 2022; Andreasson & Riveiro 2014 †; Analysis Function; Chapters 4, 10

rule: A felt distribution and a funnel carry their reading in their title and their band and n in words beside the shape
why: The public has no schema for either; a distribution is a slow glance

rule: A choropleth shows rates, never counts; its breaks are declared and, "when possible", held constant across every view of the same measure; its legend is matched
why: "standardised rates, not absolute values"; "matched legends across series … increased map-comparison accuracy by approximately 28 percent"

rule: Breaks by quantile unless a declared reason; five bands
why: Quantiles best in the one controlled test; the design system's default is natural breaks

rule: Small areas are given size — an inset, a tile form or a second view — and the map's sentence says what the darkest shape means
why: "small areas were missed by approximately 30–40% of map users"; 93 per cent chose the darker map without a legend and about half with one; the remedy is the chapter's, since the study endorses none

rule: Cartograms are used knowingly: contiguous over rectangular, and never as the only map, since a choropleth with circles beat them in the one head-to-head
why: "Rectangular cartograms are a clear outlier"; "choropleth/graduated circles are more effective" (secondary)

rule: The stigma check runs on every map before publication: no red or dark for low; large empty areas do not dominate; missing is not zero; the held category is coarsened
why: Chapter 10's rules; dark-is-more measured

rule: Two tests are run on every first screen. The two-readers test: one reader given the authored account alone and one the views alone, each asked what the place is like. The three-phones test: a reader of each user group asked, on their own phone, what the dashboard says, which figure it rests on and what they would do next
why: The field's test gap; the design systems' "test with users"

rule: The dashboard measures its own use as how, not who; publishes it aggregate and dated; and reads "those who interacted did better" with the confound named
why: "not about who uses it"; publishers "unwilling to share internal metrics"; "an artifact of participant engagement, or an effect of interacting"
source: Chapter 10; Hohman et al. 2020; Mosca et al. 2021

rule: A dashboard has a retirement plan: a banner six months ahead, the state preserved, data and metadata kept and marked, code archived in public
why: The lifecycle's fifth stage; every stated cause of a retirement read was supply-side

rule: Scrollytelling and other editorial forms sit above the dashboard, carry its states and snapshots, and are priced as unevaluated for comprehension
why: Recall equal to video and worse than text per second; scroller v stepper no difference; "it doesn't hide content"
source: Schneiders 2020; McKenna et al. 2017; The Pudding 2017

rule: Every figure about a place states its unit, the unit's vintage, and what the unit hides
why: No official unit was designed around recognition; the unit can change the finding
source: ONS geography pages; Flowerdew; Decision Book geography rules

rule: The landing unit is a declared choice; the administrative unit is shown beside it
why: The reader's officer, funder and councillor live in the administrative unit

rule: A place with no administrative edge is shown as a core and bands of agreement, with the number of people whose agreement it is
why: People judge membership of a vague region and disagree about its edge

rule: Where residents' or a scene's own units are gathered, the prompt, the sample and the consensus rule are published
why: The drawn unit was a sixth of the programme's target area and varied by place

rule: A reader may draw their own unit, subject to the query-time walk
why: The official body already allows it

rule: Comparisons across boundary vintages carry an explicit lookup
why: Best-fit carries error

rule: The reader's place is found first and by a name people use
why: Readers judge a chart by whether they find home in it

rule: The missed column is shown first, as a declared endorsement, and never alone
why: The first thing shown is read as an endorsement; no evidence speaks to the order of two true columns; assets sit beside needs, never instead

rule: "Never repeat the opposing frame" is not a reason for any layout
why: The familiarity backfire effect is not robust; frame strength decides, not count; the corrections literature tests belief, not frames, so the mechanism is weakened rather than refuted
source: Lewandowsky et al.; Swire-Thompson et al.; Chong & Druckman

rule: Both columns get the same type scale, chart quality and space
why: Space and finish are read as importance
source: Decision Book LAY-08; Wood et al.

rule: Every hole in either column is rendered at full size with its kind named by symbol and in words
why: A gap drawn over reads as data; the shorthand exists; whether an unlabelled gap reads as less value is a reading

rule: The missed column shows its intervals, samples and bands
why: Quantified uncertainty has only positive or null effects on credibility
source: Gustafson & Rice; van der Bles et al.; Chapter 9

rule: Two unlike measures never share an axis, and the cost of separate panels is accepted
why: The standard does not recommend dual axes; the house makes that a bar; juxtaposition almost never wins for precise comparison
source: Analysis Function; Few; L'Yi, Jo & Seo

rule: The bridging sentence says one thing from each column and no relation the data do not hold
why: No guidance exists; the worded-comparison rule is the model

rule: Identity fields are never ranked, and the data contract records which fields are identity
why: Scale type follows the question; the house declares its question

rule: A profile is small multiples of linear marks in a fixed, stated axis order, never a filled area; the form is held open to test
why: Radar read worst and the flower chart was preferred, in abstracts; filled area is a ranking by an arbitrary order; linear read best in the one full study, on one series
source: Albo et al. †; Feldman †; Waldner et al.; Javed et al. †

rule: Any label for a place or type is written without blame — literal, not pejorative, neither negative nor positive, naming what happened to an area — and carries the per-place hedge
why: The classifier's published naming rule, and its own output's limit
source: Gale et al.; ONS classification pages

rule: Conditions are shown as conditions with numbers, never folded into a type's name
why: A label for a condition cannot be neutral

rule: Every cross-place condition chart carries the gate's status, the harmonised criteria and the wording rule inside its frame
why: Comparability is a quality dimension producers must state; the frame is what travels
source: ESS Code P14; Code 3.0 6.6–9.3; Style Guide §12

rule: Each condition on its own spread, the place marked, the comparison worded by a published threshold
why: The official service's form

rule: Incomparable conditions are not added; the sentence says ahead-on-this, behind-on-that
why: Adding them is Chapter 5's composite by another name; the diagrams that show partial orders are hard to read

rule: The advocacy sentence passes through the gate and names its peer by method
why: Its first half is a comparison

rule: No ordering the house makes in discovery is by size or popularity
why: A sorted list concentrates exposure and changes what it sorts
source: Singh & Joachims; Salganik, Dodds & Watts; Abdollahpouri et al.

rule: A match is made from the reader's weights or nearness, shows the weights, and exists only on request
why: The careful tools show only the reader's own ordering, behind the reader's choice

rule: Every match shows its why as content cues, never as social proof
why: Content cues enable accurate assessment; neighbour cues inflate by 0.74

rule: Explanations are tested for decision quality, not liking
why: Personalisation raised satisfaction and hurt effectiveness; the founding study found no decision gain

rule: An adjacency row is a probe, not a rule, and is measured
why: Novelty lowered satisfaction; the filter bubble is unsupported
source: Ekstrand et al. 2014; Arguedas et al.

rule: Whether a kind of place is findable is a status of the category, set with the forum, recorded in the safeguards record, never a marker on a named room or business
why: Chapter 10 retired consent to be found
source: Chapter 10; opt-in directories as precedent only

rule: The Form 696 test is run with the walk before any category is made findable
why: Findable to audiences is findable to enforcement

rule: The money view says that a gap in grants data is also a gap in publishing
why: The data are what was published

rule: Any "absence made visible" method publishes its weights, its standardisation and its judgement steps
why: The official method is a composite with staff scoring inside

rule: Every chart carries, inside its frame, title, unit, source, base, address and snapshot date, for comparisons the gate and wording, and for either column the bridging sentence; the page text repeats them
why: Charts travel as screenshots; context beside the frame is cropped; a cropped counted panel must still say what sat beside it
source: Lisnic et al. 2023, 2025; Decision Book DAT-18, DAT-21, TBL-17; Chapter 11

rule: The departure from official practice on text in images is made in addition to page text, never instead
why: The standard's reason is accessibility; the house keeps the accessible route and adds the frame

rule: No screen carries an ordered all-places list
why: The thing most easily cropped into a verdict

rule: Any rank the house ever lets out carries the official wording: ordinal, relative, no distance
why: The bodies that publish ranks say so

rule: Every place-page is shown to people from the scene before publication, in a form chosen with them; what was said and what changed is recorded by role, never by name; the page says it was reviewed
why: The house's own test; the one recorded harm of member checking is the unanswered portrait
source: Style Guide slides; Candela; Data Walks; CBPR principle 7

rule: Every place-page keeps a standing errors channel and dates its corrections
why: The nearest UK case of a statistical unit made recognisable did it this way

rule: Harm through a place's representation is assessed as Chapter 10 requires, in proportion, with the measured size of the penalty stated beside the theory
why: The one field experiment reached found a small, non-significant penalty against a large theoretical literature

rule: The recognition record, ten lines, sits beneath every place-page
why: Nine records now; whether one document is for the end

rule: How the holes are drawn; how the columns are composed; the profile's visual language
why: Open, within the rules above

rule: One page per layout; the accessible routes are supplementary content on it; no parallel accessible version
why: A page conforms whole or not; an alternate version is the standard's fallback

rule: The phone layout conforms as a page in its own right
why: "A full page includes each variation … for various screen sizes"

rule: Every chart has a short description that identifies it and a long description, in body text, carrying its statistics and trend, with the data in a table where practical
why: 1.1.1's own chart example; G92; what blind readers rank most useful

rule: The long description is two to eight plain sentences generated from the current state by a published rule and read by a person against the figures; it is never duplicated in an alt attribute
why: Interviews; audit of alt texts; the anchoring finding; "auditory clutter"
source: Jung et al.; Chintalapati et al.; Mack et al.; Analysis Function

rule: The chart's description carries the chart and not the author's interpretation; interpretation lives in the authored account on the page, read by everyone
why: Blind readers emphatic against interpretation in the description; sighted readers rank it highly; both read the account

rule: Every view has a native HTML table twin with header cells, paginated and keyboard-sortable, the figures reachable before any script
why: The type most often rated accessible; the official fallback; the APG prefers native tables
source: Fan et al.; APG; Analysis Function

rule: A map's twin is joined by a sentence for the shape and the statement says the twin does not carry geography
why: Tables lost to a text map on geographic questions

rule: A navigable structure is built on graphics-document and native roles, never invented ARIA; tested with named screen readers before release
why: "A role is a promise"; "No ARIA is better than Bad ARIA"; ARIA pages carry more errors

rule: The structure is built after the description and the table, and tested against them
why: The one study's table was easier than its richest prototype

rule: Each line, slice or mark that carries meaning has 3:1 contrast unless labels carry the same information
why: 1.4.11's chart cases

rule: Colour is never the only carrier; legends match by more than colour
why: 1.4.1; declared in most of the dashboard statements read

rule: Chart text is text: SVG or HTML, never canvas; resizable to 200 per cent and respaceable
why: 1.4.4; 1.4.12 "canvas implementations of text are considered to be images of text"

rule: The frame's identifying text (title, unit, source, base, address, date; gate and wording on comparisons) is drawn as SVG text on the page, repeated as HTML beside the chart, and baked into the export; never the image alone
why: 1.4.5 is met "where both are presented to the user"; the one declared failure was a title in the image only

rule: Everything is operable by keyboard with no trap; focus visible, sized and contrasted to 2.4.13, and never covered by the filter bar
why: 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 2.4.13 (AAA, adopted); the first and third commonest public failures

rule: Nothing fires on mouse-down; every drag has a single-pointer alternative; targets 24 px or the table twin
Auto-updating views can be paused; moving content that lasts more than five seconds can be stopped
why: 2.2.2, which applies regardless of conformance

rule: The reduced-motion preference is honoured and motion from interaction can be disabled
why: 2.3.3's vestibular reason, adopted though AAA

rule: Content reflows at 320 CSS pixels; only the map and the table are excepted, not their headings or controls
why: 1.4.10 and its limit

rule: A filter changes content, not context; one polite status message says what changed; the view is never announced
Numbers are reinforced with words; each step carries what the last knew; uncommon terms are explained within one click; the "how this argues" page has a lower-secondary summary
why: COGA's patterns, specific where WCAG is silent

rule: Body type is a sans serif at a size between the two measured figures, the choice recorded; no font designed for dyslexia is relied on
why: Sans serif, monospaced and roman read better; the dyslexia fonts neither helped nor hindered in three studies; 18 point against 12–14
source: Rello & Baeza-Yates; Rello, Pielot & Marcos; Kuster; Wery & Diliberto

rule: No overlay widget
why: Practitioners rate them ineffective; a regulator's order against one vendor's claims

rule: The house publishes an accessibility statement in the public sector's model form with the twelve lines, per view, dated within twelve months
why: It is the chapter's record and what a public body's own statement can point to; the model is the regulator's form, adopted

rule: Non-compliances are declared by criterion in the public sector's form, with the route around each
why: The public sector's own practice; "statement of non-conformance"

rule: The house claims no disproportionate burden, and never on time, knowledge or priority
why: The public sector's own exclusion, adopted as a house line

rule: Tooling is chosen against these rules in week one
why: Canvas and closed tools cannot be retrofitted; official statements name the tools

rule: Chartability's critical heuristics before every release; a full pass per major release
why: Two to eight hours; evaluated on auditors' confidence, so not instead of the walks

rule: A scan, the three walks and the question before every release: scanner for contrast and the 30–40 per cent; keyboard; zoom on the phone layout; screen reader with pass criteria; a blind reader asked for the trend, the figures and, on a map, where
why: The failures found by hand and by scanner; what blind readers want asked

rule: Observed testing includes disabled readers of the real audience
why: "user research must include disabled people"; "User testing should be carried out"

rule: Audio is a labelled extra after the description and the table; recorded sound on a page, if any, is content and not a route to a figure
why: Point estimates with training; unfamiliar; of limited value for maps

rule: The distribution argument is recorded once, as funding and reputation
why: Reg 4(2)(e); the three statements

rule: The law is cited by section with its date, and never as advice
why: The chapter's own rule

rule: How the routes look and sound; the reduced-motion page; the structure's narration style
why: Open, within the rules above

rule: Sort every element into a layer, then run the removal test on every expressive one — mono, silent, still, undressed — and the fifth check: stripped and dressed say the same thing
why: Expressiveness is "all the facts" and "only the facts"; a lost fact is a wrong sort, an added fact is a false fact
source: Mackinlay 1986; Kosara 2007; W3C 1.1.1; AF infographics; ONS animations; AF §10

rule: Record each element in the boundary log, eleven lines, before it ships
why: An unlogged break is indistinguishable from negligence at the next audit

rule: Name the purchase in the affective-intent template, limited to what expression is measured to buy
why: Engagement, mood and recognition are measured, and memorability in Chapter 3; empathy, giving and accuracy are not
source: Lee-Robbins & Adar 2022; Boy 2017; Morais 2021; Kineticharts; Arunkumar 2023

rule: The precise twin is one step away and the form states its finding, and any distortion, in words on itself
why: A twin beside a form is not thereby read
source: Ottley 2019; Decision Book Ch 7; Fanning & Raworth 2025

rule: Humanised marks are whole units and are never priced as buying empathy or action
why: A sliced person encodes a fraction the data does not say; the measured effect on a hypothetical allocation is at best about 3 in 100
source: FT Visual Vocabulary; Boy 2017; Morais 2021; Correll 2019

rule: A dark register ships with a light one and the reader's choice is honoured
why: Positive polarity advantage in both age groups at small sizes; chart polarity individual; the floor already carries user override
source: Piepenbrock 2013; Dobres 2017 †; While & Sarvghad 2024; AF colours; Chapter 13's floor

rule: A drawn or approximate register is worn only where the data is imprecise, and says so
why: Sketchiness works as an uncertainty cue

rule: Mood is carried only in channels that encode nothing
why: Palette moved feeling more than the data's trend did

rule: Any sound that is content has a text document; captions include non-speech sound; nothing autoplays beyond three seconds without a stop
why: Level A

rule: A specific sensory experience is identified in words, never ignored
why: The standard's third category

rule: The conventions of objectivity are earned by the records beneath them; a source line points to a reachable source
why: The source line "performs the rhetorical, persuasive work of ascribing transparency"

rule: Never make the evidence layer harder to read on purpose
why: Disfluency: recall d = −0.01; slower; less confident
source: Xie et al. 2018; Weissgerber 2024 †; Hullman 2011 (the proposal)

rule: A headline read in passing has its letter height set from the distance it is read at, and its finding restated in the body text at arm's length
why: The legibility index; three or four words a glance

rule: Short headlines; the count is the house's
why: The mantra; the measured numbers are distance, seconds and glance

rule: The display's genre is the house's to choose; the evidence layer passes the removal test in any genre
why: Prototypicality is about speed of judgement; unfamiliar forms cost glances and liking

rule: No form is invented without a glance-cost estimate and a plan to measure it
why: One radial form took about six times a bar's glance, in one study

rule: Audit accuracy, then the floor, then beauty; beauty is never a licence
why: The field's prize has no accuracy criterion; the regulator's casework is about encodings, sources and context

rule: Probes meet the evaluated exception's standard and add a comparison
why: Logs plus survey, open materials, behaviour against self-report; no control

rule: Everything else in the register — palette beyond the encoding, display type, illustration, pattern, imagery, pacing, the poster layer, stoppable sound, disableable motion
why: Free, under the rules above

rule: Measure trust, if at all, with a fixed question in waves, of those able to express a view; never report an on-site percentage as trust
why: Producers' trust is measured this way; displays' almost never; the self-selected figure has no n

rule: Every metric has a documentation page with fixed headings — definition, rationale, method, caveats, source, frequency, date — and, where it has them, numerator, denominator and polarity
why: A reader can check what a figure is before reading it; the regulator lists sources, status, limitations and update schedule as the minimum

rule: Keep a dated, labelled change log apart from the refresh, with issue and resolved paired
why: A reader can see what changed when and why; the dashboard teams' lesson, under trust, was to disclose errors as they happen

rule: Keep the house's own errors in a machine-readable errata file and its sources' revisions in a dated list with reasons
why: A reader can tell whose mistake moved a figure; no reader evidence, so a bet with a small cost

rule: A revision is a scheduled change; a correction is labelled as a correction; print the typical revision's size once it can be computed
why: The ONS's distinction and practice
source: ONS revisions policy; GDP first estimate 2026

rule: Keep every published data file as a dated vintage from the first release
why: Results change when figures do; it cannot be started later

rule: Draw a late-returns series by event date; state the incompleteness window on the metric's page; mark it on the chart with the direction of bias; keep the by-publication series labelled as not a trend
why: The documented answer to the tail that looks like a fall

rule: Colour a value as a judgement only when it is significantly different from a named comparator; a neutral colour by default; a neutral ramp where there is no good direction; print the one-in-twenty sentence
why: A colour is read as a verdict; the RAG guide's rule and its warning that one in twenty is chance
source: PHE RAG guide 2017; OHID technical guidance

rule: Draw an arrow only under a printed rule — independent points, a stated test, a robustness check — dated where the arrow is; otherwise no arrow, with the reason
why: An arrow is a claim about a trend; rules that live elsewhere get lost
source: Fingertips trend markers; OECD user guide; Wales 2026; Scotland's redirects

rule: Show uncertainty as a range beside a point; never a verbal hedge alone
why: Ranges cost little or no trust; hedges did little for understanding

rule: Mark provisional, revised and forecast values in square brackets, not symbols
why: Screen readers find symbols hard; the UK standard

rule: Any ordering of places ships with a question-and-answer text saying what it can and cannot be used to say, with worked examples and the reason comparability is lost between editions
why: A rank implies a distance the data do not measure; the deprivation indices say so

rule: Where no composite is made, print the refusal and its reason; where one is made, its rank carries an interval
why: The OECD's sentence; the JRC's audit
source: OECD RWB user guide; JRC/GII 2024; Chapter 5

rule: A base-year index freezes its standardisation, prints the count of indicators whose change could not be measured, and carries a status notice when it stalls
why: The Health Index's method, and the notice it lacks

rule: Label every "what difference did it make" claim with its evidence level, with a declared minimum
why: Before-and-after is description

rule: Print, on any indicator display, what it is not, that no mechanical inference may be drawn from it, and the data cut-off date
why: The systemic-risk board prints all three; the other regulator displays read print the first

rule: Publish a release calendar at least a quarter ahead; release at one moment; list anyone who sees a figure early
why: The statutory test is trust

rule: Count reach in the unit counted and name it, never as "readers"; measure use only by asking, and print the response rate
why: The units do not convert; the two evaluations that asked had a 5 per cent response and a sample of survivors
source: JHU, UKHSA, OWID figures; Scottish Government 2024 (read once); Ismail 2022

rule: Write the retirement plan before launch: notice, reason, archive, licence, stable URLs, successor, gap analysis
why: Four documented endings and one undocumented; the regulator lists the plan among the minimum and asks for archiving processes "from the start"
source: OSR 2025; JHU; OWID; UKHSA; CTP; TAA

rule: Evaluate a pilot independently before roll-out, with N, n and response rate printed, and read the result before making the thing piloted a condition
why: The culture sector's own evidence: a pilot whose data were "interesting" rather than "useful" and whose benchmarking most doubted was made a condition anyway

rule: Record every borrowed mechanism in the precedent record, nine lines, with its status, before it ships
why: A rule with no stated reason is a habit; one with no evidence or named cost is a bet

rule: Which of section 9's mechanisms beyond the above to adopt, and when their conditions are met
why: The offer, with terms

rule: Establish the tier from the register before arguing about a decision; if the tier cannot be found, the register has failed, not the argument
why: The house's first move, verified at its source; "An untiered rule cannot be argued about productively"

rule: Fixed has three senses in the register — requirement, sequence, statement of the record — and every Fixed rule carries the first or the second, the third naming a truth listed apart; a rule with a hard order and an open form carries both tiers
why: The tables used Chapter 0's two senses twice and never, and two undefined ones 192 times; eleven rules were tiered differently because chapters tiered different parts

rule: Everything the chapters called "Fixed as a stance" is Adaptable (house default) unless its grounds show a requirement
why: A stance is the house's position with its grounds, which the Decision Book calls Adaptable; treating it as Fixed is deference

rule: The strongest word is used sparingly: the Fixed register is short enough to be read and its requirements are enforced by the build; the long list is Adaptable and its departures are logged
why: "Imperatives … must be used with care and sparingly"; acceptance falls 30 per cent per extra rule fired; the severe rules are obeyed where set apart

rule: A Standard in the register says whether it binds the studio or is adopted
why: Chapter 0's rule, met in eight of 241 rows

rule: A Fixed rule resting on a dagger carries the status *full text not read* and the build lists it
why: Chapter 0's rule, carried by no row

rule: A deviation is classified ignorant, lazy, expedient or earned by section 4's definitions; ignorant is logged against the register, lazy is a breach, expedient is logged and cheap to reverse, earned is the entry's nine lines
why: The house named the classes and never defined them; the fields define the forbidden grounds

rule: Two reasons never earn a departure: the maker's convenience, and the existence of a reasonable alternative that was not taken
why: The coding standard's two forbidden grounds; the accessibility guidance's "lack of time or knowledge"

rule: A departure from a Fixed rule has a deviation entry written before it ships, in the same change, with a checker named before the entry is written who is not the author; the build fails on a departure without one
why: Records born "accepted" record conclusions; records are kept where updating them is part of the change

rule: The deviation entry has nine lines — rule and tier; trigger; alternative and the one declined; buys and costs; test and result; who decided and who checked; date; review; status — stated once in section 11, and every other mention points to it
why: Five printings in three forms in the house and a fourth in this book; "A value stated twice has already begun to diverge"

rule: A departure from an Adaptable rule is logged when made and not gated; the stale-record report lists entries without a review date
why: "The job" is to depart with a record; the review date is what the house's four lines lacked

rule: Every entry and every section of the record carries a review date or a lapse condition, and the build lists the overdue at each build
why: Near-universal in the regimes read; statements not reviewed in a year; waivers not reviewed in ten

rule: An accepted entry is never edited; it is superseded by a new one and kept
why: The ADR convention, the versioning rule and the changelog's warning

rule: The log is one file with three types — departure, expressive element, borrowed mechanism — sharing the nine-line spine; the boundary log and the precedent record are the second and third types
why: Three growing lists with the same concepts under different names

rule: The twelve records are one record of the dashboard, written once per concept, kept in the repository, with ten sections (the two logs join the deviation log), one date convention, one status vocabulary per thing, one review line per section and one "what this changed" line; its public and producer's views are generated
why: "each concept is only reported upon once"; a date in twelve records under twelve names; three lines the chapters call one field
tier: **Fixed** (requirement) · publication of the producer's view Adaptable, the house's

rule: The record's public view begins with status and what is not met
why: The partial-conformance sentence and the model statement both begin so

rule: The record has a maintenance section answering who maintains it, where errors go, whether older versions are kept and how obsolescence is communicated; the service section's retirement plan is the last answer
why: The datasheet's section; the limits section is the one left empty

rule: A line that cannot be filled says "not done"; the build counts them
why: The claim and comparison records' rule; 17.4 per cent of limits sections filled

rule: The form of a break's test follows the tier's sense: a requirement by the check that can fail; a sequence by a record check of dates; an Adaptable departure by the reader the rule protects, or an adversarial walk
why: Twenty-seven of 55 tests are reader tests and two chapters lead with a removal; the chapters tied form to tier without saying so

rule: Four build checks fail the build — crop, recipe, state-honesty, removal — and two reports list: stale records and the register's statuses
why: Version 1's three, re-based; "a rule that can be measured is a rule that is run"

rule: The fifteen chapters' checklists fold into the register's test column and the build's checks; what remains as a checklist is short and is used, not ticked
why: Checklists worked where used as a team practice, not where mandated and self-reported at 98 per cent

rule: The eleven tier conflicts and five pulling rules are resolved as section 7 states; Chapter 11's headline row is marked superseded
why: Resolved as readings of the chapters' own grounds

rule: ARG-12 is carried as *disputed*, with Chapter 12's rule beside it, until Carly decides
why: A direct conflict is not resolved by the book

rule: The book's marks are rendered in the reader as bracketed words — [abstract], [secondary], [read once], [two passes] — and the dagger is a manuscript convenience
why: The Analysis Function's advice against symbols; the house's floor
source: AF symbols guidance (read once, via Ch 15); Ch 13

rule: Chapter 0 is revised as a transcription of section 7's eleven decisions and adopts the two tests for a canonical truth and the three positions on the face
why: Last revised after Chapter 2; seven chapters asked

rule: The regime's cost to the maker is counted in the build's first release
why: Not priced anywhere in the book; "will necessarily impose overhead"

rule: Whether the producer's view, the log and the parameters are published is the house's, with the regimes' default and the shuttle's exception before it
why: Publication by default in the regimes read
